stories.title: Luka Dončić scores 43, leading Lakers over Suns for eighth consecutive win, tying for NBA's top record
stories.summary: Dončić has scored 40 or more points in seven of the 12 games he's played this season.
stories.detailText: Luka Dončić continued his scorching start to the 2026-27 NBA season, topping the 40-point mark for the seventh time in 12 games in the Los Angeles Lakers' 131-123 win over the Phoenix Suns on Sunday. He currently leads the NBA in scoring at 38.6 points per game. Dončić scored 20 of his 43 points in the first quarter, hitting three 3-pointers as he shot 5-for-10 and the Lakers took a 33-24 lead. That advantage increased to 54-37 with five minutes to go before halftime on a Jake LaRavia 3. Yet the Suns closed out the second quarter with a 12-3 run to trim the Lakers' lead to 61-54. what is wrong with Luka Doncic pic.twitter.com/6mNVNH0Mi3 — Steve Jones (@stevejones20) November 15, 2026 In the third quarter, the Lakers started hot from behind the arc, hitting three 3-pointers (two by Quentin Grimes) as part of a 13-3 run and boosted their lead to 20 points. Eventually, that margin became 31 points with under two minutes remaining in the quarter. Dončić added 12 points to put him at 37 points going into the final 12 minutes. Phoenix recovered to give the Lakers a game in the fourth quarter, hitting four of six 3-point attempts to begin the frame. A Walker Kessler tip-in dunk restored the Lakers' advantage to 113-92 with just under nine minutes remaining. Jordan Ott... why has Koa Peat been sitting on the bench all year??? Koa is difference maker! pic.twitter.com/qd3dzkQqvz — Ben (@TheHurricaneBen) November 15, 2026 However, the Suns responded with a 15-1 surge, fueled by six points from rookie Koa Peat. A 3 from Ryan Dunn cut the Lakers' lead to 117-111 at the 4:40 mark. Collin Gillespie drove to the basket for a layup that pulled Phoenix to within five points with 1:05 left in regulation. But another 3 from Grimes effectively put the game away for the Lakers and Dončić closed out the scoring with two free throws. However, he told sideline reporter Roqui Theus afterward that the plan was for him to sit out the fourth quarter until the Suns made the game close. "I wasn't planning on playing the fourth quarter," Dončić said. "We gotta get better at that… Once we get up, we gotta stay there." Luka tells Roqui he wasn’t planning on playing in the 4th quarter in his post game interview vs the Suns 👀 pic.twitter.com/tWQcrxNgmj — Missy 🏄‍♂️ (@missysinghsongs) November 15, 2026 The Lakers played without Austin Reaves, who missed the game due to a bone bruise in his left heel . Overall, Dončić shot 13-of-28 from the floor, while making 12 of 14 free throws. He also notched 9 assists in his 43 minutes of play. Grimes followed with 22 points, shooting 5-for-6 on 3-pointers, with 6 assists and 2 steals. Collin Sexton contributed 16 points off the bench and Kessler added 14 points with 12 rebounds. For the Suns, Gillespie finished with 26 points (shooting 5-for-10 on 3s), 4 assists and 4 rebounds. Luke Kennard added 18 as the Suns got 78 points from their reserves. Devin Booker led the Phoenix starters with 17 points and 7 assists. The Lakers have won eight consecutive games and improved their record to 12-2, tying the San Antonio Spurs for the NBA's best record . (The Spurs defeated the Utah Jazz on Sunday, 110-102 .) Their next game is Tuesday versus the Charlotte Hornets (4-9).

stories.title: Which NBA players have the most triple-doubles of all time?
stories.summary: Russell Westbrook holds the NBA record for most triple-doubles in a career. See who else joins him on the list.
stories.detailText: Russell Westbrook has more than earned the nickname Mr. Triple Double. In basketball, a triple-double is when a player compiles a double-digit total in three of five statistical categories (assists, blocks, points, rebounds and steals) over the course of a game. Blocks and steals were officially recorded by the NBA starting in the 1973-74 season. No player in NBA history has recorded more triple-doubles than Westbrook. On May 10, 2021, Westbrook became the NBA's career leader in triple-doubles, tallying 28 points, 13 rebounds and 21 assists for the Washington Wizards in a 125-124 loss against the Atlanta Hawks . It marked the 182nd triple-double of Westbrook's career, passing Oscar Robertson for the most on the all-time list. Assist your wardrobe with NBA gear from Fanatics Nikola Jokić also has since passed Robertson, whose record stood for more than 47 years. Westbrook had already broken Robertson's record for the most triple-doubles in a single NBA season (41), recording 42 during the 2016-17 campaign. Here is a look at the players with the most triple-doubles in NBA history: Russell Westbrook*, 209 Nikola Jokić *, 201 Oscar Robertson, 181 Magic Johnson, 138 LeBron James *, 125 Wilt Chamberlain, 109 Jason Kidd , 107 Luka Dončić *, 90 James Harden *, 82 Domantas Sabonis *, 69 Larry Bird, 59 Giannis Antetokounmpo *, 58 Fat Lever , 43 Draymond Green *, 33 Ben Simmons *, 33 Bob Cousy, 33 Josh Giddey *, 32 Rajon Rondo , 32 John Havlicek, 31 Grant Hill , 29 Michael Jordan , 28 Elgin Baylor, 26 Clyde Drexler, 25 Walt Frazier, 23 Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, 22 Bill Russell, 22 *Active Check out the ESPN NBA hub page for the latest news, analysis, scores , stats , schedules and more.

stories.title: Celtics set franchise mark with 42-9 lead over Mavericks after one quarter
stories.summary: The Celtics led the Mavericks 42-9 at the end of the first quarter Sunday, the largest scoring margin in a quarter since 1987.
stories.detailText: BOSTON -- The Celtics led the Dallas Mavericks 42-9 at the end of the first quarter Sunday, marking the franchise's largest lead at the end of the period in franchise history. It's the best scoring margin by any team in any quarter since 1987, when the Los Angeles Lakers outscored the Sacramento Kings 40-4 in the first quarter. It's also tied for the third-best mark by any team in a quarter in the shot clock era, according to ESPN Research. The Celtics have led by at least 40 points in two other games this season, against Charlotte on Nov. 6 (46 points) and Chicago on Oct. 26 (40 points). Playing on four days' rest, the Celtics sprinted out to a 24-4 advantage, with Derrick White (11) and Jordan Walsh (eight) scoring 19 of those points. The Mavericks, who lost in Cleveland on Saturday, looked sluggish throughout the opening period Sunday, missing 16 of their 18 field goal attempts and going 0-for-8 from the 3-point line. By contrast, Boston shot 59% and knocked down seven 3s. The Celtics took a 67-37 lead into halftime. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.title: Darius Garland scores 27 as Clippers run win streak over Hornets to 17 with 113-105 win
stories.summary: — Darius Garland scored 27 points, Max Strus had 14 off the bench and the Los Angeles Clippers beat the Charlotte Hornets for the 17th straight time with a 113-105 victory Sunday.
stories.detailText: INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- — Darius Garland scored 27 points, Max Strus had 14 off the bench and the Los Angeles Clippers beat the Charlotte Hornets for the 17th straight time with a 113-105 victory Sunday. Derrick Jones Jr . and Isaiah Jackson each scored 13 points, while Keaton Wagler and Gradey Dick had 12 apiece as the Clippers overcame a 13-point deficit in the third quarter to win for the third time in four games following a 1-7 start. Coby White scored 21 points and Naz Reid added 17 for the Hornets, who lost for the eighth time in their past nine games and fell to 0-2 at the start of a four-game road trip. Coach Charles Lee was ejected when he received a pair of technical fouls in a 17-second stretch of the third quarter. The Hornets haven't defeated the Clippers since Nov. 18, 2017. Their last road win in the series was Feb. 28, 2009. While still awaiting the season debut of Brandon Ingram (heel), Los Angeles continued to turn things around after its poor start to the season despite being outrebounded 46-37, while taking 18 fewer shots from the floor than Charlotte. Christian Anderson had 16 points for Charlotte, which shot 38% from the floor on 92 attempts. The Clippers shot 55.4% on 74 attempts and were 51.6% from 3-point range. The Hornets led 70-57 with 6:23 remaining in the third quarter after a three-point play by White. The Clippers closed the quarter on a 22-10 run to take an 84-83 lead into the final period. The game was tied at 90 with 9:33 remaining when the Clippers went on a 10-0 run that was capped by a running layup from Dick with 6:57 remaining. stories.title: Lakers almost blow 31-point lead before escaping Phoenix with a victory
stories.summary: Lakers had a 101-70 lead late in the third quarter before holding off a furious Suns rally. Luka Doncic finishes with 43 points.
stories.detailText: Luka Doncic reacts during the first half against the Phoenix Suns on Sunday. (Kelsey Grant / Getty Images) The 31-point lead the Lakers built late in the third quarter looked insurmountable, especially with the tear Luka Doncic was on. But the Lakers learned that no lead is too big in the NBA and the Phoenix Suns were out to show them that. Though the Lakers began to reel as their lead was sliced to five points late in the fourth quarter, they were able to withstand their own inequities and the onslaught from the Suns to hold on for a 131-123 win over Phoenix on Sunday afternoon. Doncic led the Lakers with 43 points and nine rebounds and Quentin Grimes had 22, including a bank-in three-pointer with 32.2 seconds left to ice the game and send the Lakers to their eighth straight win . The Lakers led 101-70 with 1:47 left in the third quarter, the game looking over. But after the Suns cut the lead to nine points in the fourth, Lakers coach JJ Redick called a timeout with 5:02 left. Read more: While tied for NBA's best record, Lakers believe they can be better Out of the timeout, Ziaire Williams was called for an offensive foul, leading to a turnover. Ryan Dunn hit a three-pointer and the Lakers’ lead was down to six points. The Suns got to within 126-121, but after Grimes got an offensive rebound, he eventually scored on the three-ball for the Lakers to escape. Earlier, Doncic drilled a three-pointer in the face of Suns defensive ace Dillon Brooks and backpedaled down court smirking, his head bobbing and weaving while Phoenix was calling a timeout with 6:57 left in the first quarter. Even with three days off since the Lakers last played a game, Doncic was still in a groove and in his bag, his first-quarter scoring binges still a real thing. Doncic had 20 points in the first quarter, going five for 10 from the field, three for seven from three-point range and seven for eight from the free-throw line in the first 12 minutes. He leads the NBA in first-quarter scoring (13.6) and in scoring per game (38.6). Matisse Thybulle of the Lakers blocks the shot of Devin Booker in the first half Sunday. (Kelsey Grant / Getty Images) This was just another masterpiece for Doncic, who was serenaded with “MVP” chants from some fans inside Mortgage Matchup Arena after he scored, was fouled and made the free throw for a three-point play with 33.9 seconds left in the third. Walker Kessler did his thing all game long with a double-double of 14 points and 12 rebounds. Collin Sexton , who suffered a right orbital laceration in the fourth quarter of Wednesday night’s game at Milwaukee, wore protective glasses when he entered the game with 3:58 left in the first quarter and gave the Lakers a lift from that point on. But before the first was over, Sexton had taken the goggles off. Soon after, he scored on a floater while being fouled with 50.1 seconds left in the first. He finished his shift with 16 points. The Lakers actually began this trip a week ago, starting with three games that began in Detroit and went through Atlanta in a back-to-back game and finishing at Milwaukee last Wednesday. The Lakers then had three days off before going back on the road in Phoenix. They came here on a seven-game winning streak and were showing good signs of what Redick wants his team to build along the way. Read more: Lakers' Austin Reaves considered day-to-day with heel injury “We all want the good results, but what we’re trying to do is build an identity and I think our offense, advantage creation, organization, that stuff has been good,” Redick said. “I think that’s been reflected in our offensive rating. Still need to do a better job managing the ball. And then defensively for us, I think we’re building a real identity of being a disruptive basketball team. Still think we can be better with our shifts, we can be better with our rotations, we can be better at staying out of scrambles. “But like the disruptiveness is part of who we are and I think that’s something we just frankly haven’t had since I’ve been here and it’s a big part of what’s helping us win.” Lakers guard Austin Reaves missed the game with a left heel contusion/bone bruise. Reaves, who is averaging 24.7 points per game and 4.7 assists, has been “improving” since he was first injured last week in Milwaukee. “It really comes down to just like a pain tolerance thing,” Redick said. “Again, nothing structural beyond a bruise and so I think every day it’s been better and we’ll see where he’s at in 48 hours when we play on Tuesday.” The Lakers play Charlotte on Tuesday at Crypto.com Arena. Sign up for our weekly newsletter on all things Lakers. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

stories.title: Luka Doncic scores 43, Lakers stretch winning streak to 8 with 131-123 win over Suns
stories.summary: — Luka Doncic scored 43 points and the Los Angeles Lakers stretched their winning streak to eight games by holding off the Phoenix Suns 131-123 on Sunday.
stories.detailText: PHOENIX -- — Luka Doncic scored 43 points and the Los Angeles Lakers stretched their winning streak to eight games by holding off the Phoenix Suns 131-123 on Sunday. Los Angeles played without second-leading scorer Austin Reaves due to a bruised heel suffered against Milwaukee on Wednesday. It did little to slow down the NBA's top scoring team — through three quarters. The Lakers led by 31 late in the third quarter, but the Suns charged back in the fourth behind Collin Gillespie . He scored 12 of his 26 points in the final quarter and pulled the Suns within 126-121 on a driving layup with 1:05 left. Phoenix got no closer. Quentin Grimes banked in a 3-pointer with 34 seconds left and Doncic sealed it with two free throws. Doncic, the NBA's leading scorer, hit five 3-pointers and went 12 for 14 on free throws for his sixth 40-point game this season. Grimes went 5 of 6 from 3 to finish with 22 points. Suns leading scorer Devin Booker had 17 points, but shot 4 of 14 from the floor and missed all four of his 3-pointers. He did not play in the fourth quarter as the Suns rallied. Doncic showed no limitations after rolling his ankle against the Bucks, having a hand in the Lakers' first 10 points with eight points and an assist. Doncic was 4 of 9 from the 3-point line and had 25 points by halftime. Phoenix labored at both ends while falling into an early 17-point hole, but chipped away to pull within 64-54 at halftime. The Lakers stretched the lead to 20 in the opening five minutes of the third quarter and kept pouring it on before the Suns fought back. Up next Lakers: Host Charlotte on Tuesday. stories.title: LeBron James dishes 11 assists in 76ers win, passing Kidd for third in NBA ranks
stories.summary: LeBron James moved past Hall of Fame point guard Jason Kidd for third on the NBA's career assists list with 12,092.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- As LeBron James leaped for a contested layup over the outstretched arms of Indiana Pacers forward Pascal Siakam and guard Aaron Nesmith on Sunday, James turned and passed the ball to Sixers guard Tyrese Maxey for a 3-pointer. It was a pass that only James knew was coming, and it was one of eleven assists in Sunday's 131-124 win over Indiana that moved him past Hall of Fame point guard Jason Kidd for third on the NBA career assists list with 12,092. "It's super humbling. It's something that I didn't obviously foresee in my career," James said. "But I knew assists meant a lot to me. Just the movement of the ball, being able to find my teammates and put the ball on time and on target." James finished Sunday's game with 15 points, 11 assists and seven rebounds. The eleventh assist, which pushed James past Kidd, came in the fourth quarter on a pass to guard VJ Edgecombe . James has thrived as a passer against the Pacers this year, posting his top two assist totals of the season against them -- including 10 against Indiana on Oct. 28. Throughout the night, James had a handful of highlight-worthy dimes. There was a no-look pass to a cutting Jaylen Brown that drew roars from the crowd at Xfinity Mobile Arena, as well as the pass to Maxey. James said that his new teammates adjusted to his passes by necessity, after James "hit them in the head a couple times," with passes throughout training camp. "You can ask VJ [Edgecombe] for sure. I hit VJ a couple times," James said with a smile. But he and Maxey have trained together in the offseason for the last six years, so they have a different level of chemistry, James said. But even Maxey wasn't sure that the pass in the first quarter was coming. He stood ready in shooting position but then dropped his hands as James rose before quickly adjusting as the ball headed toward him. "I knew once I got his defender to stare at me, I was going to 'Rese," James said. "It caught 'Rese by surprise. He was like, 'Yo, I didn't even believe that you was gonna pass the ball.' So you know, I just tell my guys, I mean, 'Always just pay attention to me when I got the ball because I definitely see plays develop before they happen.'" A few minutes before that play, Maxey and James had a failed connection. On the opening possession of the game, James threw a bounce pass to a cutting Maxey, who missed the layup. "I missed at the rim because ... I was just jogging through and I was not playing to get the ball," Maxey said. "And the ball hit me in my chest, and I looked up; I was at the rim, so I laid in, and I missed it. But it's just like plays like that where you need to be ready at all times." James could continue to climb the charts this season, as he is 461 assists away from passing point guard Chris Paul for second all time. The top spot, held by former Utah Jazz point guard John Stockton , is a ways away at 15,062 assists. For the season, James is averaging 15.1 points, 7.2 rebounds and 6.9 assists per game. The Sixers play the Nets in Brooklyn on Monday. James hasn't played both games of a back-to-back this season.

stories.title: LeBron James climbs to third on NBA all-time assists list, passing Jason Kidd
stories.summary: LeBron James climbs deeper into the NBA record book by passing Jason Kidd for third on the all-time assists list in the 76ers' win over the Pacers.
stories.detailText: LeBron James continues to make history. The NBA icon passed Jason Kidd to move into third for most assists all time in pro basketball. He did so during the Philadelphia 76ers 131-124 win over the Indiana Pacers on Sunday, Nov. 15 at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia. James' 12,092nd assist came with 1:19 left in the fourth quarter. Dean Wade passed the ball to James, who was standing near the free throw line. James quickly tossed the ball up to VJ Edgecombe , who took two steps under the basket and slammed a dunk. LEBRON JAMES PASSES JASON KIDD 🚨 ASSIST NO. 12,092. THIRD ALL-TIME IN ASSISTS FOR LBJ! pic.twitter.com/p5LBQeY9v7 — NBA (@NBA) November 15, 2026 James spoke on how passing the ball has been a foundational part of his game from the beginning. He is now playing in his 24th season, an NBA record. "From the moment I picked up a basketball when I first started playing like recreational basketball, five-on-five, I always got a joy and a kick out of seeing my teammates score," he said on the NBC Sports broadcast after the win. "It was a feeling that felt really good about me being able to help one of my teammates out. ... Yeah, I got a kick out of that from day one." James needs 461 assists to pass Chris Paul, who sits in second place on the assists list with 12,552. John Stockton holds the NBA record with 15,806 assists. James is already the NBA's all-time leading points scorer. "It means I had a lot of great teammates," James said of reaching the assists mark. "You gotta have teammates that can put the ball in the hole. My job is just try to put it on time, on target. Lead 'em to the hole either from layups, dunks, threes, midrange, whatever the case may be. "Any time I'm on any list in NBA history, I love the history of the game. I love the players that came before me. It's super honorable." The landmark assist was one of 11 that James had on the night. He added 15 points and seven rebounds to his stat line. Jaylen Brown led Philadelphia with 31 points, two rebounds and two assists. Tyrese Maxey added 27 points, four rebounds and six assists. Pascal Siakam had 31 points, two rebounds and two assists for Indiana in the loss. James joined the 76ers this offseason after leaving the Los Angeles Lakers . In his time in Philadelphia so far this season, James beat the defending champion New York Knicks in the season opener and helped with a 29-point comeback against his hometown team, the Cleveland Cavaliers . stories.summary: Jaylen Brown, Tyrese Maxey, and LeBron James lead the Sixers to high-scoring victory over Pacers.

Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Bell Ringer Standings: Tyrese Maxey – 3.5 VJ Edgecombe – 3 Jaylen Brown – 2.5 Joel Embiid – 1 LeBron James – 1 Anfernee Simons – 1 Dean Wade – 1 No nap, no problem for the Sixers. They defeated the Indiana Pacers 131-124 on Sunday afternoon, moving to 11-3 on the season. Joel Embiid was out with plantar fasciitis management, and LeBron James returned to action following his absence against the Raptors. The Sixers’ interior defense let the Pacers run up their total in the first half, but the Sixers’ offense proved too much for Indiana in the latter half. Three Sixers finished with six or more assists in what was a transition-filled effort. Let’s get to Bell Ringer. Jaylen Brown: 31 points, 12-of-18 FG, 3-of-6 3PT, 5-of-6 FT, 2 assists, 2 rebounds, 1 steal Jaylen Brown came out the gates firing against Indiana, making seven of his first 10 shots and scoring 16 points through the first 14 minutes of game time. Most of his work came in the midrange, creating space from the defender with the fadeaway and draining it time and time again. He showcased his pose and ball-handling in the post, understanding that the double team likely will not come to help, and using his length and athleticism to get the shot over the defenders. His focus appeared reengaged after last week’s dud against the Celtics and sloppy night against Toronto on Thursday. He nabbed a steal early in the first half, and made three of six attempts from deep. Jaylen Brown is up to 16 points on 7/10 FG pic.twitter.com/zPVRk3dVnE — Liberty Ballers (@Liberty_Ballers) November 15, 2026 It was Brown’s most efficient scoring game of the season. Tyrese Maxey: 27 points, 9-of-19 FG, 5-of-10 3PT, 4-of-5 FT, 6 assists, 4 rebounds, 1 steal Maxey continues to be the ringleader for the squad, intersplicing his speed drive, pullback crossover and step back to keep the defense off balance. His change of pace ability allows him to stay a step ahead of the defense, and his supporting cast lets him take advantage of the space he creates with ease. Paired with his marksman ability to shoot, the Pacers were effectively unable to guard him. Maxey found success at all three levels on Sunday. His passing has also been crucial to the Sixers’ offensive success, and he displayed it tonight with six assists. He found multiple guys in transition, but none better than this lob to LeBron James on a fastbreak. LeBron, LeBron, LeBron 🎶 pic.twitter.com/4hGfnABYRG — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) November 15, 2026 LeBron James: 15 points, 5-of-8 FG, 5-of-6 FT, 11 assists, 7 rebounds, 1 block His passing ability opens up the floor for everyone, and was evident against the Pacers. With his 11 assists, he passed Jason Kidd on the NBA’s all-time assists leaders. He added crucial buckets inside and helped push the pace for the Sixers in transition. James is doing everything his body is allowing him, filling lanes in transition and hitting cutting teammates with slick bounce passes on multiple occasions against Indiana. stories.title: I owe Sam Hauser an apology
stories.summary: Hauser is the third longest tenured Celtic for good reason, as one of the drivers behind their early success.
stories.detailText: BOSTON, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 04: Sam Hauser #30 of the Boston Celtics looks on during the second half against the Milwaukee Bucks at TD Garden on November 04, 2026 in Boston, Massachusetts. The Celtics defeat the Bucks 109-102. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images I’ve consistently been a champion of Sam Hauser’s game since he first joined the Celtics. But I wavered. As last season wrapped up, I believed his time in Boston was probably winding down. That wasn’t about a lack of belief in his abilities, but I felt the team needed to shake things up a bit, and his contract would give them the easiest pathway to accomplish that. The other reasoning was that they could distribute his minutes to some of their younger wings to fully understand what they’ve got there. The problem with that analysis is that it undervalues a long sample of Hauser being flat-out awesome. To start this year he’s been as good as ever. After a “down year” shooting 39.3% from three, he’s currently hitting a career-high 43.5%. He’s fourth in the NBA in three-point attempt rate, reestablishing himself as one of the league’s top marksmen. With a very fluid offensive approach for Boston this year, Hauser has played a big part in their on and off-ball screening game. He’s been the recipient, flying around stagger screens and knocking shots down on the move. He’s also brought his usual ghost screen and pick-and-pop ability, creating advantages for himself or the ballhandler. Paul George has been an extremely natural fit next to him. The two of them have such a ridiculous amount of combined shooting ability that it’s hard for an action between them to not throw the defense off. Sam killing them with the ghost screen then draws a hard closeout. Leaves Payton completely open in the corner. pic.twitter.com/Z44efW6X0Y — Pull up shoot (@NElGHT_) November 11, 2026 They each demand so much attention on the perimeter. A brief mix-up here means the defense has to sprint in rotation to Hauser. Then they’ve left an equally deadly shooter in Payton Pritchard wide open. Hauser is a key contributor in helping Boston execute their offensive principles. Factors like maintaining proper spacing and generating 2-on-1s are some of his skills that might fly under the radar, but help the Celtics play how they want to. He’s an incredibly threatening off-ball option and has been a staple of Tatum-led bench units that historically crush teams. That’s been the case once again this year. With Tatum and Hauser on the floor, the Celtics have a +26.6 Net Rating. I try to avoid treating small samples like gospel, but for those two it’s supported by years of data. Hauser’s spacing gives Tatum more room to operate, and Tatum’s gravity gives Hauser clean looks. It’s a perfect partnership. When you think about building a great lineup around Tatum, Sam is the exact type of fit you need. It’s why I must say that I regret discussing him as a trade candidate. Knowing that Tatum would be back for a full season was enough to make me feel bullish on several players, but Hauser should’ve been thought of as the primary beneficiary of that. He’s always provided a boost to winning basketball games, and he’s playing alongside his most compatible teammate. For this season, Boston has a +20.7 Net Rating swing with Hauser in the game vs on the bench. That number is absurd and will stabilize eventually. It’s clear, though, that he is a key to their success in the early part of this season. Aside from the shooting, he’s been good enough on the defensive end to earn some high praise from Joe Mazzulla. “He’s one of the better defenders that we have on our team, because he does a great job of taking away the #1 thing…so detailed in taking away player tendencies,” Mazzulla said. He’s a player that can be on the floor in any scenario. Boston is developing their other wings to fit in that mold, but for Hauser there’s not a high-leverage moment where the team needs to sub him out. This was reinforced most recently in the Celtics grind of a win against Toronto. Wow Celtics were extremely ready for this play from the Raptors. Great switch and interception from Hauser pic.twitter.com/hHrfV2j32a — Pull up shoot (@NElGHT_) November 12, 2026 With the Celtics up three, and the Raptors looking to tie it, it was Hauser that sniffed out the play and came up with a huge steal to seal the game. The fact that he was in the game for that moment speaks to the level of trust and respect the coaching staff have in his defense. Jordan Walsh and Hugo Gonzalez have the label as stronger defenders, but it’s Hauser that’s on the floor to close it out. That’s not a knock on either of those young wings, but a testament to the level of preparation Mazzulla mentioned. For Hauser, his knowledge of the system is nearly as important as his shooting ability. This is his 6th season with the team, making him the 3rd longest-tenured Celtic. He’s reached a point where he’s leaned on for his perspective. “Overall, I have seen a lot, experienced a lot,” Hauser said. “Just trying to help younger guys… and then this year, coaches have wanted me to be a little more vocal and share my thoughts, what I’m seeing.” On a roster that had a serious shakeup, Hauser is a steadying force. You always know what you’re going to get from him. He doesn’t step outside of his role, and he executes it masterfully. While he may have a tradeable salary, it’s the value he provides on a great contract that makes him even more worthy of sticking around. The Celtics are a better and more cerebral team for having him.

stories.title: LeBron James moves past Jason Kidd for 3rd on NBA’s career assist list, 76ers top Pacers 131-124
stories.summary: LeBron James moved into third on the NBA's career assist list, leading the Philadelphia 76ers past the Indiana Pacers 131-124.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA — LeBron James had 11 assists and moved into third on the NBA’s career list, and he added 15 points and six rebounds to lead the Philadelphia 76ers past the Indiana Pacers 131-124 on Sunday. James, who turns 42 next month, dished one to VJ Edgecombe in the fourth quarter for assist 12,092 to pass Jason Kidd on the career list. John Stockton and Chris Paul are 1-2 in NBA history. Jaylen Brown scored 31 points and Tyrese Maxey added 27 for the Sixers. Pascal Siakam led the Pacers with 31 points and former Sixer Kelly Oubre Jr. added 16. James continued an early habit in his first season with the Sixers by picking his spot to take control of a game. This one came in the third quarter, right after Sixers fans went wild when seldom-used 7-foot-6 center Tacko Fall checked into the game. James immediately went to work picking apart the Pacers and scored eight straight points to give them an 82-73 lead. Fall was a factor. Signed ahead of training camp for backcourt depth, Fall almost immediately strained his left hip and missed the preseason. Coach Nick Nurse said ahead of Sunday’s game he still thought the fan-favorite Fall could help the Sixers, but that he had “seen him out there, some form,” and that “I might just have to take that leap.” Fall helped in that pivotal third-quarter stretch for James. Fall grabbed an offensive rebound that led to a possession where James would sink two from the free-throw line. James then added a near-uncontested driving layup because of a perfect screen from Fall. James added a 20-footer and a dunk during the run. Fall grabbed two offensive rebounds in 3 minutes. His final stat line with no points in 5 minutes might be easy to overlook — unlike the towering Fall — but he had a major impact in pushing the Sixers to 11-3. Joel Embiid sat out for the Sixers in the first set of back-to-back games. A two-time NBA scoring champion, Embiid should return to the lineup Monday at Brooklyn. James is another veteran who generally does not play in back-to-back games and seemed poised to take his turn sitting out against the Nets. James took a hard foul when he drove the lane against Oubre in the first quarter. James clutched his left wrist for a moment but appeared to show no ill effects the rest of the game.

stories.title: Can the Raptors break a double digit losing record against the Knicks?
stories.summary: New York comes north as Toronto will have to stop a KAT attack
stories.detailText: The New York Knicks are heading to Toronto for a two-game stretch against the Raptors, with games on Sunday and Tuesday nights. The Raptors have struggled mightily against the Knicks lately. Not only did Toronto go 0-5 against the defending champions last year, but they have a 13-game losing streak against New York, with no regular season wins against their division rivals since January 2023. And, as odd as it is to say, the Raptors may be hosting the defending champions at the right time. This year’s Knicks are sputtering along at just 6-6. Their losses have all been by single digits, but their play has been characterized by the same malaise that plagued them in the middle of last season. If Toronto is going to break the losing streak, even though Kawhi Leonard won’t be suiting up and Scottie Barnes is listed as questionable , there may not be many more opportunities where the Knicks are more vulnerable. How do the teams stack up? Let’s take a look. Know thy enemy What’s been surprising about this year’s Knicks is that they’re by and large the same squad that absolutely blitzed the Eastern Conference in last year’s playoffs. The only rotation player from the title-winning squad who has departed is Mitchell Robinson, and the team isn’t particularly old. Despite a short offseason (filled with late-night TV appearances , among other things ) and some fatigue, the chemistry that brought the Big Apple its first title in over 50 years should have carried over into the new season. It has not. NEW YORK, NEW YORK – NOVEMBER 11: Karl-Anthony Towns #32 of the New York Knicks reacts against the Cleveland Cavaliers during their game at Madison Square Garden on November 11, 2026 in New York City. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Blown pick-and-roll coverages have popped up. Opposing shooters have been afforded too much space. The offense has resorted to the sort of hero ball that led to them falling into a 2-1 series deficit to the Atlanta Hawks, with the team standing around waiting for Jalen Brunson to bail them out. Every starter not named Karl-Anthony Towns has been significantly less efficient on offence, and he hasn’t gotten the late-game touches he deserves. Last year’s team sported a top-five offence. This year, they’re just 13th, and somehow playing at an even slower pace (29th in the league) than last year. And, once again, the Mikal Bridges discourse is in full swing, with head coach Mike Brown trusting Landry Shamet over him in key moments. That being said, these are the reigning champs, masters of improbable comebacks, and they have a recent history of lollygagging for a while against the Raps, before turning it up in the fourth quarter and putting the game away, and their defence still ranks in the top five in the league, despite its flaws. On the last episode Thanks to an NBA Cup quarterfinals match, the division foes actually matched up five times in the regular season last year, with New York winning all five, by an average of 19.6 points. The Raptors struggled with injuries (and, uh, covert tanking) last year, but this was a lopsided matchup. Key matchup(s) Karl-Anthony Towns vs Jakob Poeltl and Collin Murray-Boyles and also his own teammates For much of this season, KAT has been the line bright spot in the Knicks’ starting lineup. That lineup has had its fair shares of issues over the last few seasons, before flipping a switch last postseason, and many of those old issues have reared their heads again. Towns is shooting a sizzling 54% from the field and 40% from three so far, but New York periodically forgets they employ a seven-footer who’s one of the best shooters on the planet. He possesses a unique skillset that allows him to pull Poeltl out of his comfort zone defensively, and the size to pin CMB under the basket, if his team chooses to feed him on the block. And, with the way they’ve been playing, that’s a big “if.” Even more so than Bridges, OG Anunoby, or Josh Hart getting back on track, the key for New York is making sure to take full advantage of KAT’s gifts. If the Raptors can make him a non-factor and bother Brunson enough as a scorer (it should be noted he had offseason wrist surgery and hasn’t fully been himself), the Raptors have a shot over these next two games to finally end their years-long losing streak against the Knickerbockers.

stories.title: Inside the Jordan Dome, where 'Space Jam' pickup games helped MJ get his game back
stories.summary: Thirty years after "Space Jam," those who shared the summer with Jordan remember the basketball that unfolded offscreen.
stories.detailText: Michael Jordan had seen enough. With rising UCLA sophomore and national champion Kris Johnson defending him, reigning NBA All-Star Cedric Ceballos wouldn't let the youngster go away easily. Ceballos had been "busting my ass," Johnson told ESPN, and talking smack while doing it. At North Carolina, a poster of five-time NBA All-Star Marques, Kris' father, hung in Jordan's dorm room. Jordan had recently taken Johnson under his wing. So with Ceballos picking on Johnson, Jordan took action. He would guard Ceballos and Kris switched onto another All-Star, Reggie Miller. "I'm like, 'OK, all right, what's going on over here?' And then Mike just systematically just went to attack Ceballos on multiple possessions," Johnson told ESPN. In Johnson's words, Jordan "dismantled" Ceballos with multiple buckets in a row and delivered the trash talk back. Rocking the patent leather Jordan 11s, he jab faked with the ball palmed looking down and expressing his disdain that Ceballos wore 23 in the league -- Jordan's jersey number. Johnson and Jordan won the game, a pickup held on the Warner Bros. lot in the summer of 1995 while Jordan filmed "Space Jam." The intensity of those runs rivaled a playoff atmosphere, and that interaction with Ceballos showed Johnson something. "My takeaway, wow, Mike's a crazy motherf---er. He's really in real life, he's really that dude," Johnson said. Jordan had just returned to the NBA after leaving to play baseball. The Orlando Magic defeated him and the Bulls in the playoffs, celebrating emphatically on the Bulls' home court. It marked the first time since 1990 that Jordan's Bulls didn't play in the NBA Finals. For all intents and purposes, it wouldn't be a normal offseason. Add in a potential distraction with "Space Jam" responsibilities, and Chicago's three-peat could've been one-and-done. But, this was Michael Jordan. He had Warner Bros. build the "Jordan Dome" on the lot. The six-week schedule included shooting scenes with "Monstars" by day, and hooping against the NBA's own "Monstars" by night: Reggie Miller, Patrick Ewing, Grant Hill, Charles Barkley, Shaquille O'Neal, Alonzo Mourning and more. Sunday marks the 30th anniversary of "Space Jam," which grossed $250.2 million worldwide against an $80 million budget to become the highest-grossing basketball film at the time. Jordan Brand commemorated the anniversary with a new six-part documentary that began Sunday. While the basketball on camera with the Looney Tunes drove that box-office success, the basketball played off camera helped shape Jordan's next act. The pickup games at the Jordan Dome helped prepare him for Chicago's 72-10 season and another three-peat, gave fellow players a confidence boost and, according to his longtime trainer Tim Grover, served as an informal tryout for his future Bulls teammate. "I'm not sure he played as much pickup ball in the offseason after that [95-96 season]," Hill told ESPN. "I could be wrong. ... But I think the summer of '95, it was about let me find, let me rediscover things. I don't know if he would ever acknowledge that, but I feel like it was like I got to get back to a certain level. And he did." The story of Jordan's first retirement then return is well-known. Months after winning his third straight championship, Jordan abruptly retired in October 1993, saying he had "nothing left to prove in basketball." Baseball awaited with the Chicago White Sox and its minor league squad in 1994. It required a physical with obstacles. Grover explained to him that the muscles for baseball were completely different than the muscles for basketball. He told ESPN that he "totally redesigned" Jordan's body for baseball. So when Jordan decided to return to basketball in March 1995, it seemed like His Airness would be back to his old self, but Grover believed there wouldn't be enough time to prepare his body. "I said, 'Listen, you will still be MJ, but you won't be your version of MJ.' And he was like, 'Yeah, you don't know what the f--- you're talking about,'" Grover told ESPN. "And then he goes, he comes back and has [55 points] against New York and all this other stuff. But I had spent so much time watching him. I could just see there was just a little bit of a difference." Jordan averaged 26.9 points in 17 regular season games, then put up 48 in Chicago's first playoff game against the Charlotte Hornets. The Bulls beat the Hornets in the first round, before losing in six against the Magic in the second round. The offseason brought new territory for Jordan with no championship to play for. Jordan's movie commitment happened before his basketball return. Nigel Miguel served as the film's basketball technical adviser and Jordan's body double. Miguel told ESPN that Jordan's contract included a guarantee that there would be a place and time set aside for him to work out. The idea for the Jordan Dome was born, though the studio's initial vision was considerably less elaborate. At Warner Bros. in Burbank, California, Grover met with a production official who proposed blocking off the VIP parking lot and painting basketball lines so Jordan could play outdoors. "I was like, 'This is freaking Michael Jordan. Michael Jordan is not playing basketball on a parking lot,'" Grover said. There had to be a wooden basketball court, which Long Beach State supplied. The structure also had to be climate-controlled with shower facilities, a putting green, speakers, a card table, bathrooms, running water, ice and a weight lifting area. Even the lights had to be similar to the ones used in arenas. Grover approved Warner Bros.' idea of the "Jordan Dome" and also a tweak himself: What about putting the Jumpman logo on top of it? "Michael shot that down," Grover said, laughing. But the facility passed all the tests once it was completed and included a door with a combination lock. The dome was torn down after filming so executives could receive their parking spots back. Miguel revealed that Hollywood legend Clint Eastwood took the weights -- fitting since A-list celebrities like Queen Latifah and Will Smith stopped by to watch games. Director Joe Pytka, a hooper himself, called the dome fabulous and paradise, adding it became a scene. Grant Hill said he had never seen anything like a real court "essentially on a parking lot." Twelve-year NBA pro Tracy Murray, an extra in the film, likened it to going to "a circus or something.". "Once you pull up to the actual site of the venue, which I had never seen before, it was 1995 and domes constructed like that weren't really normal," Kris Johnson told ESPN. "It looked like some weird stuff back in '95, like what the hell is this?" This was near the set of "Space Jam," after all. Next came spreading the word. Pytka had a familiarity with Jordan, as the two previously worked on multiple commercials. The shooting schedule went right up to NBA training camp, an added pressure for Pytka and the crew. Jordan's schedule was 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. Monday through Saturday with a two-hour lunch in between. Prior to arriving on set, Jordan would get shots up at 5 a.m. with Grover. There would be more work at lunch, before playing pickup in the evening until 11 p.m. or midnight. Murray emphasized that Jordan was "locked in" on coming back, and the movie wouldn't be a distraction. The cast and crew couldn't believe Jordan's daily itinerary. Stories in Hollywood often get exaggerated, but Grover ensured them: "This is who [Jordan] is." While lifting weights with Grover and building chemistry with Bugs Bunny could be seen as the appetizer, the nightly pickup games served up the main course. "Space Jam" had no shortage of NBA stars cast outside of Jordan. The "Monstars" consisted of Barkley, Ewing, Larry Johnson, Shawn Bradley and Muggsy Bogues. Others were uncredited, such as O'Neal, Scottie Pippen and Charles Oakley, according to IMDB. Grover and Jordan worked their Rolodex, calling players to let them know when the pickup games would begin. UCLA men's basketball, fresh off a national title, got an invite. Grover had final say on who would come in and out, but Miguel and Nathaniel Bellamy Jr., a basketball coordinator and utility stunt man for the film, assisted in getting the word out, too. "So it was kind of like you would tell players, you talk to their agents and whatever, 'Yeah we're casting for this part in the movie. They have that but then there's gonna be training there too. So come work out afterwards as well,'" Miguel said. The league was in a lockout during most of filming, which allowed players to arrive freely. No one needed permission from their teams, according to Grover. It also delayed the attendance of Magic Johnson, then part of the Los Angeles Lakers' ownership group. He arrived later in the summer. Murray likened the pickup runs to an All-Star Game -- a fitting comparison considering the Jordan Brand has outfitted the league's All-Star Game since 2018. Pytka participated in some games, even having an encounter with Jordan on the court. "He was coming in for a dunk and I stepped in front of him to take a charge," Pytka told ESPN. "All I felt was a breeze and he dunked over me. Now, he could have gone over me, but it seemed like he went through me like a magical thing. I'll never forget that. It was just a breeze and he went by boom. It was incredible." Grover described a revolving door of people at the pickup games, with even the invite-only crowd of stars from other Warner Bros. productions waiting behind a VIP velvet rope for the doors to open. "Michael was and still is the star of stars. The stars want to meet him," he said. "Sylvester Stallone, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Kurt Russell, Dean Cain, I mean, the list, whoever was like the most prominent actor and actresses and writers and producers. They were all wanting to meet him." The players faced a similar waiting period. With "15 All-Stars in there," as Grover put it, some of Johnson's UCLA teammates grew tired of waiting for a turn and stopped coming after a week or so. Arguably the biggest beneficiary of the runs was Dennis Rodman, whose spot on the court carried a different set of stakes: a potential future alongside Jordan in Chicago. After a seven-year run with the Pistons, the rebounding machine had spent two antic-filled seasons with the Spurs, the final of which included him being suspended and taking a leave of absence. Grover revealed that Jordan received a call from the Bulls while at the Dome asking about his thoughts on the team potentially acquiring Rodman. At first, Jordan rolled his eyes, but then inquired about bringing him to play in the pickup games. Rodman arrived and Grover deemed it Rodman's "tryout" to see if Jordan would give the green light on a deal. "If that thing did not go well, the history of Dennis Rodman and the Chicago Bulls was not going to happen," Grover said. "Cause if Michael said, no, there was no way. There was no way they were going to make that trade." Rodman passed the test and Chicago got him in September 1995. Not far from a set where Jordan faced the "Monstars," he gained one that helped him three-peat. Games followed a simple format: shirts and skins, first team to seven and the winner stayed on. That was necessary to ensure that all the big names that arrived could hit the court -- and keep the intensity high, like Jordan desired. "It was probably the most competitive seven points you were going to get. It was like a playoff atmosphere," Murray said. "You come on there half-stepping and you're done right away and you're gonna sit there for hours before you get back on. So it was a war for those seven buckets." Soon enough familiar rivals matched up again and Jordan began breathing fire. "On the court, I didn't realize how ruthless of a villain he was," Johnson said. Murray recalled it in an instant. Johnson was almost insulted by the question. "Oh please, did [Jordan and Reggie Miller] go at it?" Johnson said. A southern California native, Miller consistently attended the Jordan Dome runs. He and Jordan famously fought in a 1993 matchup. So it would come as no surprise that the two competed passionately, but especially in one game. Murray compared it to "two bulls locking horns." "I remember the day that Mike and Reggie were going at it like it was Game 7," he said. "The rest of us just threw them the ball and said, go to work because the level of trash talk during that time. They were going at each other like it was Game 7 of the Eastern Conference championship. ... I just don't see that type of love, passion and competitiveness anymore. But you saw it in a pickup game." The same occurred when Grant Hill arrived. Hill recently finished a Rookie of the Year campaign where he averaged 19.9 points, 6.4 rebounds and five assists per game. Hill was in the area due to a cameo appearance on the sitcom "Living Single," which Queen Latifah starred in. According to Johnson, an underlying conversation at the time centered on Hill's status among the game's best. Naturally, people anticipated how Jordan and Hill would match up. Hill received an invite, but only could play for two days due to his schedule. "I didn't know who would be there," Hill said. "I didn't know what the gym court situation was going to look like. I came with the hope of being able to be included and being able to play." Hill hadn't considered a matchup with Jordan until he checked the ball and found himself face-to-face with him. Hill excelled on the first day, to the point where he rang his friends to brag that he "gave Jordan the business." The following day, Jordan was "steaming," according to Grover, and instructed his trainer to put them on opposite teams. Jordan then got his revenge. "I just remember Mike and G Hill absolutely going at it. And Mike really strapping in, trying to guard, trying to defend, really took the matchup serious," Johnson said. "Grant Hill was trying to bust Mike's ass, and they both got the best of each other during the matchup. ... That was the moment of the summer for me." Before playing on the second day, Grover put Hill through a workout and the Naismith Basketball Hall of Famer said Grover "kicked my butt" in the weight room. At one point, Hill even asked Grover if Jordan trained like this, to which the trainer said yes. "I'm not sure I ever lifted that hard and then I played and so I kind of rationalized things and justified my poor performance due to Tim Grover killing me in the weight room," Hill said. "But Jordan the next day, after I lifted weights, he gave me the business and he didn't seem to miss a shot and I couldn't make a shot." Hill wouldn't jump to the conclusion that Jordan masterminded the heavy lift session to wear Hill out. But, it made its mark. "I wasn't conditioned for that at that moment. I hadn't fully bought into the strength training at that point of my career," Hill said. "But yeah, whether he told him or not, I attribute my poor performance to that." Grover, Miguel and Bellamy arranged the teams, with input from Jordan based on what he wanted to work on that day. "He was very specific in things that he was trying to do to get back to basketball shape and basketball mindset," Miguel said. On days that Jordan was running point guard, Grover would instruct a smaller person to guard and pick him up 94 feet. He would also tell them to force Jordan left, right or straight up. Teams were rotated so that Jordan could learn players' tendencies again, and it played a part in him returning to his preferred shape. "He never wanted 'best teams.' He always wanted to play against the best players or folks that would bring out certain things on him that he was trying to work on that particular time," Miguel said. After learning Johnson was Marques' son and hadn't been picked to play despite repeatedly showing up, Jordan gave Grover and Bellamy a standing instruction: Whenever Johnson came to the dome, he would be on Jordan's team. The arrangement built Johnson's confidence while giving Jordan another challenge. "He was tightening up the bringing up the ball against pressure, the facilitating. So he was drawing doubles, using his gravity a lot in those pickup runs to sort of [call out] 'Mid-post area, let me get two over here,'" Johnson said. "And he had me on his team as a weak link, I think, to make it more difficult for him to win games. There were weeks where I was the only non-NBA player on the floor." The pickup games were "an unbelievable situation" to improve in, according to Murray, and players reaped the benefits. Those brushes with greatness, as Johnson described it, led to him having his best season in college the following year. "It really kind of kick-started my entire development at UCLA and during that era." Johnson said. "Knowing I could play, knowing I was real, knowing I was good enough. Mike really instilled a lot of confidence in me that summer." A similar result occurred for Murray, who averaged a career-high 16.2 points with Toronto the next season. After limited playing time in his first three campaigns, he truly felt like he belonged in the league the next season. "I came in there confident, ready to go, because that experience of playing with those greats on the floor all at the same time," he said. "If you're out there and you're being effective and you're out there blending in and playing just as good as everybody else, of course, you reach a certain level of confidence that carries over." For as much as the participants improved their game in the Jordan Dome, Jordan himself needed an environment like that to return to form. His usual offseason regimen never included as many pickup games as that summer. But, Grover agreed that they were "absolutely one of the most critical and necessary parts" of Jordan's preparation for the upcoming season and beyond. Hill had never taken a break that long from basketball. So he struggled to understand how hard it would be to come back. That summer foreshadowed how the following three would begin for Jordan and the Bulls: with championship parades. "Those games, finding his rhythm, playing against professional-level players, I think really helped prepare him for the start of the season," Hill said. "If you recall, they were off and running. And he was back to the level of player that really kind of, I think, helped set the table for him in the next three-year championship run." A dome in Burbank helped Jordan stamp home the words he had faxed months earlier: "I'm Back."

stories.title: Embiid-less Sixers get just enough from center position in win vs. Pacers
stories.summary: Tacko Fall got his first real minutes and Jabari Walker’s strong play continued as the Sixers beat the Pacers.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 15: Tacko Fall #99 and VJ Edgecombe #77 of the Philadelphia 76ers talk during the game against the Indiana Pacers on November 15, 2026 at Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Jesse D. Garrabrant/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images It’s been awhile since we saw a 1 p.m. win on a Sunday in this city. The Sixers knocked off the Indiana Pacers 131-124 Sunday Afternoon. Jaylen Brown powered the Sixers with 31 points shooting 12-of-18 from the floor along with three rebounds. Tyrese Maxey quietly put up 27 points and six assists shooting 9-of-19 from the field. LeBron James had a tremendous day sharing the rock as his 11 assists moved him up to third in the league’s all-time assist leaders. He also had 15 points and six rebounds on 5-of-8 shooting. VJ Edgecombe bounced back from a scoreless first half to end with 11 points, four rebounds, and six assists shooting 5-of-11 from the floor. Pascal Siakam led the Pacers with 31 as well. Joel Embiid was out with plantar fascia management in his right foot, along with Adem Bona and Dominick Barlow. The Pacers were missing Tyrese Haliburton, Andrew Nembhard and Ben Sheppard. Here are some thoughts at the buzzer. First Quarter The Sixers moved the ball very well on their opening possession of the game as Maxey got wide open on a cut, but he smoked the bunny. It looked like he might not have corralled the bounce pass from LeBron. Maxey did get the Sixers on the board running quick off the ensuing Pacers miss. Brown knocked down two of his first three jumpers as the two of them accounted for Philly’s first 15 points of the game. A lot of what Maxey was able to get early was set up by LeBron, who was zipping the ball all around the perimeter early. Maxey took full advantage and had a lot of space to get his first two three-pointers off. Maxey found James up ahead for a transition bucket for James’ first points of the day. LeBron ↪️ Rese pic.twitter.com/tYtWrUjH2k — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) November 15, 2026 Brown had a really good jump shooting quarter, putting up 11 in the first. He didn’t seem to have a hard time getting to his pull-up spots, and knocked them down whether there was a hand in his face or not. Meanwhile on the other end, all five of the Pacers’ starters scored within the first six minutes of the game and started the game 11-of-19 from the floor. They were already taking advantage of the small Sixers team available with nine early second-chance points on four offensive rebounds. Kelly Oubre Jr. was playing in Philly for the first time since signing with the Pacers, and got off to a good start. He scored seven in the first, beating his old team on a couple of cuts. Another old friend, T.J. McConnell, hit a few of his classic short pull-up jumpers. The Sixers trailed by six after the Pacers shot 62% from the field in the first. Second Quarter A quick rest on the bench didn’t cool Brown down as he nailed two more jumpers to star the second. After getting some minutes in Delaware over the weekend, Labaron Philon Jr. was back in the rotation, checking in early in the second, even if it was because Anfernee Simons picked up two quick fouls. The first time he got into an action was LeBron screening and rolling for him, but the play was quickly whistled dead when Quentin Jackson got into it with James. A couple possessions later James hit Philon on the wing for a three. the rookie and the vet 🫡 pic.twitter.com/ZDBOpD80Rf — Philadelphia 76ers (@sixers) November 15, 2026 Regardless of whether the Sixers had Jabari Walker on the floor or a less traditional center option, they had trouble giving the Pacers any resistance at the rim. Fourteen of Indy’s first 16 points in the second came from the paint or getting fouled in the paint. With that shot diet it wasn’t a shock they continued to hover over 60% from the field. Brown continued to find ways to put the ball in the basket, and the Sixers needed every bit of it to keep pace. There was even a sequence where he grabbed a rebound from the floor despite getting hit in the face earlier in the possession. After a couple of fast breaks Maxey simply created with his speed. James threw a brilliant bounce pass down the baseline to Brown for another fast break that capped off a 16-4 Sixer run. Coming out of a Pacer timeout, Oubre drew a foul on a Brown push-off, something Oubre really exaggerated in celebration. Aaron Nesmith scored a basket out of that, but Oubre missed the corner three the Pacers got out of a Maxey turnover their next trip down the floor. DIMES https://t.co/dgZyjhQeeS pic.twitter.com/OZZlVqzI39 — Liberty Ballers (@Liberty_Ballers) November 15, 2026 LeBron took that rebound and got up the floor quickly for a dunk attempt before the half but Oubre fouled him hard to avoid that. James hit the deck hard and stayed down for a bit, but eventually got up and knocked down two free throws to put the Sixers up by one at the break. Whether it was related or not, James and Maxey had a lengthy discussion with Tyrese Haliburton before heading back to the locker room. Third Quarter Going scoreless in the first half, Edgecombe just could not buy a bucket. He missed another open corner three early in the third, but did start to produce. He nabbed a steal to start the quarter and found Maxey for a three, then finally got a couple of baskets himself going to the basket. He tried his damndest to put Ivica Zubac on a poster, but Zubac got over with enough time to meet Edgecombe with a hard foul. A center with a clear height advantage like Zubac was always going to give Walker trouble defensively, but he was putting in another good shift of hardwork. On top of pulling down four defensive rebounds and two on the offensive end, Walker had drilled three threes which is always a nice help to the offense. With that being said, Nick Nurse decided to give Tacko Fall his frst real minutes when Walker went to the bench. Fall rebounded Edgecombe’s missed free throw, which once again sent the crowd into a wild frenzy. They also ate up every bit of the screen he set for LeBron as James scored eight straight for the Sixers. LEBRON 3Q FLURRY IN PHILLY 🔥 Scores through traffic. Hits the midrange jumper. Throws down the alley-oop slam. He's scored 8 of his 12 PTS in just the 3Q on 3-3 FGM! pic.twitter.com/XRKSGFqlId — NBA (@NBA) November 15, 2026 There were some rusty moments like a foul and a defensive three-second violation, but the Fall minutes definitely could have gone worse defensively. Multiple shots at the rim were altered by him being there, including a layup attempt that went out of bounds over the backboard. Their defense to close the quarter looked more comfortable. Dean Wade made a great play to stop a fastbreak, and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope fought for a loose ball that led to him earning a pair of free throws. Maxey fell into a rhythm again on the other end, hitting a floater and another stepback three. Simons hit his second quarter-ending buzzer-beater in as many games, giving the Sixers a 10-point lead after the third. Fourth Quarter After such a strong first half Brown had to sit most of the third quarter when he quickly picked up his third foul. That long rest didn’t slow his momentum down though as he hit a pull-up to start the quarter before trailing LeBron to hit an open three off the catch. A few possessions later Edgecombe made a nice read to open up Wade in the corner, setting the Sixers up to good position to start running away with the game. A three from Josh Huff followed by two consecutive and-1s by Siakam made sure that this game was far from over. The Sixers responded with a possession of great ball movement that, as the tweet below points out, was entirely orchestrated by LeBron, and led to another Wade three. However Siakam answered again by getting right to the basket and would pick up another and-1 two possessions later. Sixers go with Weave action into an advance to LeBron. VJ Edgecombe comes from the right wing to screen. Watch LeBron call for Wade to go from the block to the left corner. No switch, Edgecombe gets it and drives. Huff pulls into help, kick to Wade for 3. pic.twitter.com/2dvKbXoyv8 — Steve Jones (@stevejones20) November 15, 2026 The Sixers’ offense did stagnate a bit, especially when LeBron went to the bench. They were lucky they weren’t punished more during their two minutes scoreless stretch. The only time they stopped Siakam in this stretch was when he pulled up for a jumper. Brown was finally able to snap that with a midrange but the Pacers were still able to chop the lead to four. KCP hit a big three to push that lead back up as LeBron was waiting to check back in. James threw another dime to a baseline cutter on his first possession back in the game, and Wade was able to draw a foul as he finished the dunk, putting the Sixers back up by double-digits with just over two to go. After Brown split a pair of free throws, Siakam got another and-1. He missed the free throw, and after each team committed an offensive foul, that pretty much put the Pacers in fouling territory from there on out.

The Celtics need to defend him well and avoid giving him open shots. The Celtics also have to be aware of his defense as he is very good at deflecting the ball and getting steals. He is shooting 47.9% from the field and 39.0% from beyond the arc. He has long carried a grudge against the Celtics, even going so far as to stomp on the logo after a game at the Garden and so always gives his best effort to try to beat them. He is questionable due to the back to back and for injury management and so if he can’t start, I’m guessing that Marcus Sasser gets the start in his place. Honorable Mention Jayson Tatum vs PJ Washington, Jr Washington is averaging 14.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 1.1 assists per game. He is shooting 41.8% from the field and 35.1% from beyond the arc. The Celtics need to keep him out of the paint and off the boards. They also need to avoid leaving him open on the perimeter. Keys to the Game Defense – Defense is always the number one key to winning games. There is no truer statement than “Defense wins Championships.” The Mavs have an offensive rating of 112.5 (16th) while the Celtics have an offensive rating of 117.4 (6th). The Mavs are 12th with a defensive rating of 111.7 while the Celtics are 2nd with a defensive rating of 105.6. When the Celtics struggle on offense, as they sometimes do, they have to be able to stop the other team from scoring. The Celtics especially need to defend the paint as the Mavericks average 48.3 points in the paint per game. The Celtics have to continue to make defense their identity. Rebound – Second to defense, rebounding is the key to winning. One of the few times I have agreed with Pat Riley was when he said “No rebounds, no rings.” The Celtics are averaging 44.8 rebounds per game (8th) while the Mavs are averaging 44.0 rebounds per game (15th). The Mavs are 6th with 16.5 second chance points per game. The Celtics need to put out extra effort on the boards to keep the Mavs from getting extra possessions and second chance points and to give the same to themselves. Be Aggressive – The Celtics must be the more aggressive team. They have to be more aggressive in going to the basket, in diving for loose balls, and on defense. They have to aggressively crash the boards. They have to be the team that wants to win the game more. They absolutely can’t let the Mavericks play harder than them if they want to win this game. Hard work beats talent when talent doesn?t work hard and when talent works hard, they are very hard to beat. Move the Ball Carefully – The Celtics are at their best when the ball moves and they make the extra pass. When the ball sticks and players try to do too much, the Celtics struggle. But they have to make careful passes and not get sloppy because the Mavericks average 18.4 points off turnovers and 17.2 fast break points per game. The Celtics need to be careful with their passes and ball handling because if they aren’t the Mavericks will make them pay. X-Factors At Home and Rest – The Mavericks will be on the road and playing on the second night of back to back games. They will have the distractions of travel and playing in front of a mostly hostile crowd,although I expect a lot of cheers for hometown Cooper Flagg. Fatigue could be a factor for the Mavs while the Celtics have had 3 days off and should be well rested. The Celtics need to get motivation from the home crowd and defend their home court with energy and effort. Officiating – Officiating is always an x-factor in every game. stories.title: Fred VanVleet is Rockets unsung hero
stories.summary: The Rockets’ Fred VanVleet has proven himself to be a winning player.
stories.detailText: AUSTIN, TX - OCTOBER 23: Fred VanVleet #5 of the Houston Rockets shoots the ball during the game against the San Antonio Spurs on October 23, 2026 at the Moody Center in Austin, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Fred VanVleet is a postmodernist. Hear me out. The point guard position has undergone a radical transformation over the last decade and a half or so. Like any seismic change, it’s hard to pinpoint a precise catalyst. When Derrick Rose became the youngest MVP in NBA history in 2011, that was a watershed moment. His 7.7 assists per game were point guard-y enough, but the 25.1 points per game would have imposed a “shooting guard” label on him at any other point in league history. Rose was the new meta. Houston Rockets fans know the change intimately. Firstly, Mike D’Antoni’s decision to run the offense almost exclusively through James Harden was another critical juncture. Fast forward, and we’re arguing ad nauseam about whether Kevin “I am obviously not a point guard” Porter Jr. is a point guard. Here’s what makes VanVleet postmodern: He’s a throwback, in a sense. Ball security is his superpower. VanVleet facilitates in a low-risk, medium-reward way. Yet, he’s also modern. VanVleet launches pull-up threes that would make Mark Jackson blush. It’s the only means he really has of bending defenses, and modern, starting-caliber point guards must bend defenses. At times, those shots can look a little bit absurd in the moment: But in the bigger picture, they’re part of what makes VanVleet so impactful. Rockets’ VanVleet is a winning player I love when people do the work for me. Fred VanVleet has the best assist to turnover ratio in the NBA this season amongst all starting point guards. He’s averaging 5.4 assists with only 1 turnover a night. In addition to that, he currently has a career high 60.3 TS%, and a team high +10.2 (+/-). pic.twitter.com/j71mN14sAW — Bradeaux (@BradeauxNBA) November 14, 2026 Thanks, Brad. DataBallr has VanVleet’s impact as even more positive, with a +14.1 On/Off split. I’m not sure why different outlets calculate on/off stats differently, but what matters is that the stats consistently demonstrate that VanVleet is a winner. VanVleet’s True Shooting % (TS%) is buoyed by his combined three-point volume and efficiency. He’s hitting 39.5% of his 7.4 threes per game. For this Rockets team, that’s priceless. Many have suggested that Alperen Sengun would thrive if paired with a more dynamic point guard. It would be easy to point out that (again, per DatalBallr) the duo is +13.8 when they share the floor, but there are solid normative explanations for their success as well. Just as VanVleet is not Jamal Murray, Sengun is not Nikola Jokic. He’s a less natural shooter, and he’s not on Jokic’s level as a passer. That’s not a knock: Sengun is a top-ten (and closer to five) passing big man in NBA history, but Jokic is a top-ten (and closer to five, and really closer to two or three) passer in NBA history. But Sengun is perhaps a better ball-handler (it feels ethically necessary to note that he’s a much better defender here, but it’s not relevant here). That ball-handling ability makes him one of the best isolation bigs in the NBA, but some of Sengun’s pick-and-roll finishing looks a lot like isolation basketball too. I’ve said this before, but Sengun and VanVleet run the pick-and-roll like Stockton and Malone. Often, the purpose of the set is largely to advance Sengun’s position by a few inches before he starts cooking. It’s a job that, say, Kyrie Irving is overqualified for. That’s not to say that outright that the Rockets shouldn’t trade for him (for example, although it feels like he’s the only star guard they’re at all likely to acquire). There’s a part of me that thinks the 2026-27 team is our best window, and more pure offensive firepower is what we need. There’s another (and ultimately, I think, stronger) part of me that thinks VanVleet’s willingness and ability to let Sengun cook is what’s best for his continuing development. The stats strongly suggest that VanVleet makes Sengun better, and the Rockets, in general, a better team: That’s as close to an objective truth as one could possibly find.
