stories.title: Week 5 Look-Ahead: Stephen Curry and Caleb Wilson go down, and toss Jeremiah Fears the keys
stories.summary: In another eventful week in the NBA, there were key injuries, a trade request and a historic performance from Cade Cunningham.
stories.detailText: By the end of Sunday's game, four weeks will have passed in the 2026-27 season. Unfortunately, we've got more injuries to key players to deal with, and there has also been a trade request. Most NBA players won't become trade-eligible until December 15, so it remains to be seen whether there's significant movement before then. Let's look at some of the key storylines from Week 4 before moving on to Week 5. Five Week 4 Storylines - Warriors lose Stephen Curry: After a 0-3 start, the Golden State Warriors looked nothing like a team capable of being a factor in the Western Conference. They then ripped off eight straight wins, thanks to Stephen Curry's continued greatness, rookie Yaxel Lendeborg being ready for the moment and a supporting cast offering consistent contributions. Unfortunately, the momentum came to a screeching halt during the Warriors' November 11 loss to the Rockets, as Curry suffered an oblique abdominal tear in the first quarter. He'll be re-evaluated in a little under two weeks, but the injury could keep Curry sidelined for close to a month. The November 13 game against the Spurs was Golden State's first since Curry's injury, and it was not good. In the 123-85 defeat, Lendeborg shot 1-of-13 from the field, scoring three points, and Brandin Podziemski (eight points) wasn't much better, making two of his ten attempts. Those two will need to step up in Curry's absence, with the Warriors beginning a four-game Week 5 on Monday in New Orleans. - Caleb Wilson injury shifts the ROY race: While the Bulls haven't started the season well, losing nine of their first 12 games, Wilson's play has been a bright spot. The rookie forward is averaging 18.9 points, 6.2 rebounds, 1.9 assists, 1.8 steals, 0.9 blocks and 2.3 three-pointers per game. Unfortunately, he fractured his right hand during the Bulls' November 11 loss to the Spurs and is expected to miss four to six weeks. In their first game since Wilson's hand injury, the Bulls beat the Hawks in overtime on November 13. Isaac Okoro (15/3/2/1 with two three-pointers) moved into the starting lineup, while Norman Powell (33/5/2/1 with four three-pointers) and Josh Giddey (15/10/14 with three blocks and three three-pointers) had highly productive nights. Two players to watch after Wilson's injury are Matas Buzelis and Patrick Williams . The former appeared to have trouble finding his place in the Bulls' starting lineup with Wilson on the floor, while the latter has moved into the rotation after racking up DNP-CDs early in the season. - Cade Cunningham historic night: Cunningham had a career night in the Pistons' November 12 double-overtime win over the Wizards, going off for 52 points, five rebounds, 11 assists, one steal, one block, three three-pointers and zero turnovers. Not only was this his first 50-point game, but this was also the first time since the NBA began tracking turnovers in 1977-78 that a player finished with at least 50 points, 10 assists and no turnovers. “It was the best I’ve ever done it in my NBA career, for sure.” Cade Cunningham (52 PTS, 11 AST) on how well he felt like he minimized mistakes and maximized effort after becoming the first player to record 50+ PTS and 10+ AST with ZERO TOs since 1977-78 in the Pistons’ 2OT win!… pic.twitter.com/Kyo6ZrVhOn — NBA (@NBA) November 13, 2026 After averaging 4.4 turnovers per game in 2024-25, Cunningham's average has decreased each of the last two seasons, down to 3.2 per game in 2026-27. His play is a big reason the Pistons enter Week 5 with an 8-4 record, good for third in the Eastern Conference. - Dejounte Murray requests a trade: The Pelicans' roster felt awkward when the team opened training camp, due to the mixture of veterans whose long-term outlooks with the franchise were a bit cloudy and young players who needed room to figure out who they can be as potential building blocks. That led to Murray and second-year guard Jeremiah Fears starting together, and New Orleans began the season with four straight defeats. Murray was away from the team for personal reasons in late October, and New Orleans went on a three-game win streak with Fears running the show by himself. The Pelicans went 1-4 after Murray's return, and on Thursday it was announced that his representation requested a trade. Pinning the Pelicans' struggles solely on Murray would be unfair, but it was clear something needed to change. Officially, Murray has missed the last two games with a sprained ankle, but it's difficult to envision him playing another game for the Pelicans. Not only does this boost Fears' fantasy value, but it does the same for Herb Jones , who has returned to the starting lineup. - Paul George steals the show in Jayson Tatum/Jaylen Brown duel: Tuesday's game between the Celtics and 76ers was the first regular-season meeting between the teams since the offseason trade that sent Jaylen Brown to Philadelphia and Paul George to Boston. Of course, the main storyline was the relationship between Brown and Jayson Tatum , but PG-13 stole the show. In 30 minutes, George dropped 36 points, five rebounds, one assist and six three-pointers, shooting 14-of-22 from the field. He did not play against Toronto the following night, but the only two games George has missed so far were for injury management. George played 78 games total in two seasons with the 76ers; if he stays relatively healthy, that would be a game-changer for the Celtics and for fantasy managers who grabbed him with a middle-round pick in drafts. Five Week 5 Storylines - The Lakers could be without Austin Reaves: Reaves suffered a contusion and bone bruise in his left heel during a November 11 win over the Bucks. Despite the Lakers not having played a game since, the guard was ruled out for their November 15 matchup with the Suns. The good news for the Lakers is that Quentin Grimes is available after missing the Milwaukee win with a finger injury; he could be the player asked to fill the void in the starting lineup. Ziaire Williams , who began the season as a starter, may also see his opportunities increase after Jake LaRavia jumped ahead of him in the pecking order. The Lakers play three games in Week 5, beginning with a home back-to-back against the Hornets and Jazz on Tuesday and Wednesday. Between Reaves and Luka Dončić , fantasy managers rostering either player may not get full value because of injury or injury management. - Franz Wagner carries a four-game streak of 30 points or more: The Magic forward has been outstanding recently, scoring at least 30 points in four straight games. In his most recent appearance, Wagner recorded 35 points, nine rebounds, 12 assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in a November 13 win over the Bucks. While the schedule has been forgiving, with Orlando following up an overtime loss to the Warriors with wins over Sacramento, Utah and Milwaukee, that shouldn't take away from Wagner's play. And with Paolo Banchero (ankle) not due to be re-evaluated until late November, Franz has more room to take control of things offensively. - The Celtics, Mavericks and Knicks have the busiest weekends: Boston, Dallas and New York will play games on both Saturday and Sunday to end Week 5. From an injury-management standpoint, Boston's Tatum, George, and Dallas' Kyrie Irving are the players most likely to be affected. Players like Payton Pritchard (Boston), Naji Marshall , and Zaccharie Risacher (Dallas) may find themselves in positions where they can take on more responsibility than usual. The Knicks may have the most forgiving back-to-back of the three, as both of their games will be at home. Boston ends its west coast trip with games against the Kings (prime resting spot?) and Warriors, while Dallas hosts the Clippers on Saturday before visiting the Jazz the following day. - Seven teams will have the weekend off: Among the teams that won't play on either Saturday or Sunday to end Week 5 are the Cavaliers, Rockets and Lakers. Due to a back-to-back, made worse by Friday's travel issues caused by the FAA, Cleveland didn't play any of its starters on Saturday against Dallas. In one of the most impressive performances of the season, the Cavs won. Tyrese Proctor recorded a triple-double, Meleek Thomas scored 20 points, Mario Hezonja scored 22 and Thomas Bryant recorded a double-double. Kenny Atkinson's team plays games on Monday, Wednesday and Friday, so the stars will get a little more rest in a good schedule week for them. As noted above, the Lakers could also use a weekend to recuperate from recent injury issues. Each of the seven teams that don't play on Saturday or Sunday will be active on Friday, so the end of those games is when fantasy managers should move on from players who aren't considered "must-roster." - The Trail Blazers get to play another back-to-back against the same team: After hosting the Thunder for games on Tuesday and Wednesday of Week 4, winning both, Portland begins Week 5 with games in Minnesota against the Timberwolves on Monday and Tuesday. For the Blazers, Damian Lillard played both games of the Thunder back-to-back, logging 24 minutes in a 20-point win on Tuesday and 32 in a 10-point win the following night. His ability to play back-to-backs coming off of the Achilles tendon rupture is encouraging, but the nature of the first win over Oklahoma City likely helped, as Lillard didn't play at all in the fourth quarter. ‍♂️ Three Questions 1. Will the Pelicans find a trade partner for Dejounte Murray this week? 2. Will "Wingstop" get back to business in New York? 3. Which team ends its losing streak first: Milwaukee (L9) or Utah (L11)? stories.title: Pacers-Nets back-to-back could push Sixers’ frontcourt depth to its breaking point
stories.summary: The Sixers don't have a single healthy center against the Pacers on Sunday other than Tacko Fall. This is fine!
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA, PA - NOVEMBER 12: Tacko Fall checks into the game against the Toronto Raptors on November 12, 2026 at the Xfinity Mobile Arena in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and/or using this Photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by David Dow/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Heading into the season, frontcourt depth behind Joel Embiid looked like a legitimate concern for the Sixers. When Ariel Hukporti suffered a torn Achilles in the preseason opener, those questions ratcheted up tenfold . But not even the most glass-half-empty pessimist could have anticipated how dire the Sixers’ frontcourt situation would be for Sunday’s game against the Indiana Pacers. Embiid is out with “right foot plantar fascia injury management,” which is no surprise since it’s the first end of a back-to-back. Dominick Barlow is still dealing with the low back stress reaction that has delayed his season debut. Adem Bona is out at least for another few days with a cervical spine strain. And Hukporti is obviously out as well, barring a medical miracle in the next few hours that can instantly cure torn Achilles tendons. Jabari Walker, who stands 6-foot-7, figures to draw the start at “center” for the Sixers. The other options at head coach Nick Nurse’s disposal are 6-foot-9 forwards LeBron James and/or Dean Wade, along with two-way signee Tacko Fall. Walker is a strong rebounder and does what he can to make up for his lack of height, but he provides almost zero rim protection. The Pacers figure to force the issue down low with Pascal Siakam and Ivica Zubac all game as long as those two can stay out of foul trouble. Might this be our best chance yet for Tacko Time? He played three minutes in the blowout loss to Cleveland last Friday and made a brief cameo at the end of their win over the Toronto Raptors on Thursday, but that’s the extent of his playing time thus far this season. Jaylen Brown, his former teammate in Boston, recently advocated for more Tacko Time, particularly given the depleted state of the Sixers’ frontcourt. Jaylen Brown: “We need some more tall people. It’d be great to see Tacko get an opportunity.” — Kris Rhim (@krisrhim1) November 13, 2026 Barlow appears to be on the mend, although Bona is facing a murky timetable to return. Head coach Nick Nurse told reporters earlier this week that Bona had seen a specialist for his injury and would be out for at least another week, which has effectively granted the backup 5 job to Walker by default for now. The Sixers have little choice but to downsize against the Pacers now, which is hardly optimal against the 6-foot-8 Siakam and the 7-foot Zubac. The Pacers might have a layup line all game, although this will force the Sixers to get creative defensively. They should look at this as an opportunity to hone their small-ball looks against traditional frontcourts and figure out counterpunches if their opponent looks to just pound the ball inside. If the Sixers do succumb to Tacko Time and give him more playing time than they have to date, that could also help them answer some questions about how they’re using that roster spot. If the Pacers drag him into every offensive action, how long can Nurse stick with him before the game slips away from them? Can he hold his own and buy them some time? If not, what’s the point in spending a two-way spot on him in the first place? We’re still a few weeks away from the Sixers being able to sign someone to a prorated veteran-minimum contract while staying under their first-apron hard cap. Trade winds are beginning to swirl now that the season is almost one month old, but the Sixers can’t include anyone whom they signed this offseason until Dec. 15, which leaves Justin Edwards’ $2.4 million contact as their best salary-matching trade bait for now. The Sixers would likely prefer to avoid having to fill their final roster spot until they get closer to the trade deadline so they can maintain as much optionality as possible. But if Barlow and Bona don’t return soon, how the Sixers fare Sunday in an Embiid-less game could help determine how imminently they need to solve their backup center issues. Unless otherwise noted, all stats via NBA.com , PBPStats , Cleaning the Glass or Basketball Reference . All salary information via Spotrac and salary-cap information via RealGM . Follow Bryan on Bluesky .

stories.title: Sixers, Brown have a ‘humbling' night in loss to Celtics
stories.summary: Jaylen Brown called the Sixers' blowout defeat to the Celtics “humbling.”
stories.detailText: Sixers, Brown have a ‘humbling' night in loss to Celtics originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Whatever Jaylen Brown and the Sixers dreamed up for their first matchup against the Celtics soon flew out the window on Tuesday night. Brown was whistled for two early fouls, the Sixers fell behind and their early-season flaws were on full display in a 123-101 loss at Xfinity Mobile Arena. “We’ve just got to get better,” Brown said. “Tonight was humbling. We got outplayed, out-executed. So we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the next one.” Over 26 minutes, Brown had 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting and five rebounds against the team that traded him away this summer. As for the endless dissection of his relationship with former co-star Jayson Tatum , Brown didn’t have much to add Tuesday. There was no public reconciliation, no obvious on-court animosity and generally nothing to satisfy fans hoping for some kind of fireworks on that front. The pregame moment between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown. 📺 NBA on NBC and Peacock pic.twitter.com/P4iclUnqZ5 — NBA on NBC and Peacock (@NBAonNBC) November 11, 2026 “I’m just focused on doing what’s best for my team,” Brown said. “Everything else … to be honest, I wasn’t paying attention. But credit to Jayson; he played well tonight. Credit to the Celtics. They executed, they shot the hell out of the ball and they were the better team tonight.” Tatum scored 21 points, two of which came on a third-quarter slam over LeBron James. Paul George continued his fantastic start as a Celtic by dropping 36 points and draining six three-pointers. The Celtics dominated from beyond the arc, shooting 22 for 49 (44.9 percent). The Sixers went just 11 for 37 (29.7 percent) on another night of underwhelming offense. The team sits 22nd in the NBA in offensive rating , 24th in three-point makes per game and 21st in three-point percentage. “I think that we’ve got some guys that are obviously shooting much lower percentages than their last season or their career average — almost a handful of guys,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. “And I don’t think it’s because they’re shooting fallaway, totally contested ones. I think they’re shots we want them to take. So I think they’ll continue to take ‘em and I’m pretty sure those will even out into their career averages.” Joel Embiid is at 37 percent from the floor and 4 for 33 from three-point range (12.1 percent). The Sixers’ seven-time All-Star center got through an injury scare when he rolled his ankle late in the second quarter and hit a three early in the third. It was his first long-range make since the Sixers’ home opener back on Oct. 22. “It’s a work in progress,” Embiid said. “I think the biggest thing is just not thinking. I’m probably overthinking it. The rhythm of the game is different. I’m so used to having to create for myself, so it’s a little bit different. “But I think I’m slowly getting better. You could see as soon as I made a three, the next shot in the short corner … I didn’t even think about it. I just shot it and let it fly, and I made it. … I think it’s just about taking what’s in front of you. Make or miss, keep working on your game. It’s going to get there at some point.” Even with the Sixers second in the Eastern Conference standings at 9-3, Embiid believes the team’s defense has “slacked off a little bit” in recent games. “I don’t really look at the record,” he said. “I just look at the process of, ‘Are we getting better every day?’ We can always do a better job at all phases of the game.” Boston’s now first in the East at 9-2. “They’re one of the top teams in the league and they’ve been together for a while,” Brown said. “We’ve got a lot to work on over here, so we’ve got to get to work.” The Sixers will face the Raptors on Thursday night in Philadelphia. They’ll have to wait until Jan. 21 in Boston to see the Celtics again. “I was looking forward to this,” Brown said. “I was looking forward to playing well, but s— happens. Just get ready for the next one.”

stories.title: Observations after Brown-Maxey duo scores 58 points in Sixers' win without Embiid
stories.summary: The Sixers improved to 11-3 on Sunday by beating the Pacers without Joel Embiid.
stories.detailText: Observations after Brown-Maxey duo scores 58 points in Sixers' win without Embiid originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Jaylen Brown-Tyrese Maxey duo starred, LeBron James reached another milestone, and the Sixers earned a win without Joel Embiid on Sunday afternoon. They improved to 11-3 on the season with a 131-124 victory over the Pacers at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Brown scored 31 points and Maxey posted 27. LeBron James had 15 points and 11 assists. He passed Jason Kidd on Sunday for third in NBA history with 12,092 assists . Pascal Siakam scored 31 points for the 5-9 Pacers. On the first day of a back-to-back, the Sixers were down Embiid (right foot plantar fascia injury management), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) , Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The Pacers’ injured players included Tyrese Haliburton and Andrew Nembhard. The Sixers will face the Nets on Monday night in Brooklyn. Here are observations on their win over the Pacers: Walker’s 1st start Jabari Walker started for the first time this season, opening the game at center. He’s been in the Sixers’ rotation the past five games since Bona’s injury. Walker set up the Sixers’ first basket, swiping a steal and then tossing the ball ahead to Maxey for a fast-break dunk. Maxey and Brown both began well and combined to score all of the Sixers’ first 15 points. Though he conceded five inches to 7-foot Pacers center Ivica Zubac, Walker was solid in his first stint. He got an early post stop on Zubac and then snatched a strong defensive rebound. Dean Wade was next up for the Sixers at the five. He sunk a three-pointer on his first shot to give the team a 20-16 lead. Walker ended up playing 25 minutes and posting 11 points and seven rebounds. Wade had 12 points and seven boards in 35 minutes. The Sixers’ lack of healthy conventional centers remained a clear deficiency. Of course, everything should be simpler once Embiid is back in action. An NBA chance for Philon The Sixers’ defense did not have a sparkling start. The Pacers tallied 35 points in the first quarter and shot 62.5 percent from the field. Brown helped the Sixers avoid a substantial deficit by draining all sorts of jumpers. He rarely appears bothered by close contests. Brown moved to 7 for 9 from the floor when he knocked down a three early in the second quarter. Kentavious Caldwell-Pope’s triple knotted the contest up at 37-all. Sixers head coach Nick Nurse needed to stray from his Plan A rotation when VJ Edgecombe picked up his third foul with 9:56 left in the second quarter. Labaron Philon Jr., who got a game with the G League’s Delaware Blue Coats on Friday night , subbed in. For a rookie guard , Philon has looked comfortable and confident on offense in most of his NBA appearances. He swished a long-range jumper in the second quarter and saw a floater rim out. Tacko time Brown reached the 20-point mark and put the Sixers up one with a slam assisted by James late in the second quarter. He ran into serious foul trouble in the third quarter. Brown was whistled for his fourth foul with 9:53 left in the period for an off-arm shove on Aaron Nesmith. Wade entered and Brown exited. The Sixers’ slim lead didn’t slip away. Walker nailed threes on consecutive possessions and Maxey jammed in a dunk. Soon after, Tacko Fall came in for his first meaningful minutes as a Sixer. The 7-foot-6 two-way contract player grabbed an offensive board off a missed Edgecombe free throw, which drew one of the day’s loudest cheers. With Fall on the floor, Maxey and James connected on an alley-oop that extended the Sixers’ lead to 82-73. Fall’s main defensive assignment was 7-foot-1 Jay Huff. When the Sixers tried to sit in a zone, he was called for a defensive three-second violation. Whatever the scheme, most of Fall’s defensive work will come around the paint. He certainly has exceptional physical traits as a rim protector and is not nimble on the perimeter. Fall logged five scoreless third-quarter minutes and recorded three rebounds. The Sixers outscored Indiana by a point with Fall on the court. Given Fall is occupying a (two-way) roster slot and the Sixers are so depleted at center, it made sense to see a bit of what he can do outside of garbage time. While five minutes isn’t enough for any grand conclusions, it’s very safe to say Fall is a unique player. The Sixers built their advantage to 102-87 with a Brown three early in the fourth quarter. They couldn’t cruise to a blowout, though. Siakam kept hurting the Sixers as a driver and had a highly efficient fourth quarter, scoring 19 points on 7-for-9 shooting. Quenton Jackson’s layup trimmed Indiana’s deficit to 119-115. The Sixers ultimately held off the Pacers’ push. Caldwell-Pope canned a three, Wade threw down an and-one dunk, and James checked off his milestone assist with a late dish to Edgecombe for a layup.

stories.title: ‘Hard to win': Simons, Walker carry Portland lessons into Sixers roles
stories.summary: Former Blazers teammates are contributing in different ways for a Sixers team built to contend.
stories.detailText: ‘Hard to win': Simons, Walker carry Portland lessons into Sixers roles originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia Anfernee Simons and Jabari Walker shared the floor for 128 games in Portland. The Trail Blazers won 43 of them. They sat beside one another in the Sixers’ interview room Thursday night after a victory and discussed what the other 85 taught them. “Whether you’ve got a big role or a small role, it’s hard to win in the NBA,” Simons said. “We’ve seen it firsthand.” Their roles were considerably different then. Simons was an established starter entrusted with creating and scoring. Walker, a 2022 second-round pick, was trying to establish himself in a rotation. During their three overlapping seasons, Portland went 33-49, 21-61 and 36-46. The Blazers missed the playoffs each year. Both are now reserves on a Sixers team constructed to contend. In nine games they’ve both appeared in this season, Philadelphia is 7-2. They provided 26 points, 11 rebounds and six three-pointers in the Sixers’ 123-112 win over the Raptors at Xfinity Mobile Arena. Simons scored 17 points and shot 5 for 6 from three-point range. Walker recorded nine points and eight rebounds, including four on the offensive glass. The Sixers outscored Toronto by 24 points during Simons’ 23 minutes. Neither former Blazer committed a turnover. Their production helped Philadelphia overcome a 17-point first-quarter deficit and improve to 10-3 without LeBron James. “You learn once you come off the bench to kind of read the game before you get in there,” Simons said. “Obviously, we started off kind of slow. You just want to go in, bring some energy, get some stops, get out and run. I think everybody who got off the bench brought energy.” Simons supplied an immediate lift with a deep three-pointer at the first-quarter buzzer. His shot ended an 8-0 Sixers run and trimmed Toronto’s lead to nine. He remained involved during an 11-0 burst late in the third quarter, knocking down a three and setting up Walker for a basket. Walker then made a three early in the fourth before Simons scored on the Sixers’ next possession. When Toronto pulled within six with less than five minutes remaining, Simons answered with his fifth three-pointer. Making those shots is the most obvious way Simons can help a roster already featuring James, Joel Embiid, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown. He said the Sixers have not made him feel as though every opportunity must go in. “They encourage us to keep shooting the ball,” Simons said. “Knowing that a team has that much confidence in us to keep shooting makes the game that much easier. Whether you miss or make, as long as we get the right shots in the right moments, I think everybody can live with the misses and makes.” Simons spent seven seasons in Portland before playing last year with Boston and Chicago. His move to Philadelphia reunited him with Walker and Rayan Rupert, another former Blazer who joined the Sixers on a two-way contract during the offseason. Knowing familiar faces awaited him helped Simons enter another new locker room. “It made the transition seamless,” he said. “Just being able to have some comfortability with guys that I played with for multiple years. It’s been fun, kind of feeling like a little bit of old times. Me, Bari and Rups have been through a lot.” Walker’s path to Philadelphia began a year earlier and required an additional step. After playing 188 games over three seasons with Portland, Walker signed a two-way contract with the Sixers in July 2025. He earned a standard contract in February and has since pushed his way into the backup-center conversation despite standing 6-foot-7. Walker believes some of the work he did on losing teams was easily missed. “When I first got to the league, I was part of a rebuilding process,” he said. “I just felt like some of the little things I did didn’t always get noticed when you’re losing. I told myself, if I ever got to be part of a winning organization, then I’d go out and expand my abilities.” Rebounding has made Walker difficult for Nick Nurse to overlook. Walker credited his timing and strong hands to lessons passed down by his father, former NBA center Samaki Walker. Those instincts have become especially useful while the Sixers piece together their frontcourt behind Embiid. “Rebounding is a skill I kind of honed in on,” Walker said. “My dad was a good rebounder. He was known for his rebounding and his timing. I think it’s just a gift that he transferred to me.” Walker has made it clear that he expected to earn a role this season. “I don’t know if I was delusional, but I always felt like I was going to play and I was going to be a part,” he said. “I read something where they said it’s a surprise, but if you were around me this summer, it wouldn’t be a surprise. This is expected, and I just want to continue to get better.” The freedom Simons once had in Portland is no longer necessary. Walker does not need a high volume of touches, either. Both understand that playing beside the Sixers’ stars requires shooting when open, moving the ball and handling the less glamorous work. “You’ve got to find ways to impact the game multiple ways, even if you’re not scoring,” Simons said. “Whether it’s cutting, making the right read and pass to Joel, being the right swing pass to VJ, boxing out on defense or just being in the right position.” Their opportunities will fluctuate. Simons may take nine shots one night and only a few the next. Walker’s minutes will depend on matchups and the health of Philadelphia’s frontcourt. Winning has changed what they are being asked to do. Their three years together in Portland taught them why the adjustment is worthwhile. “You feel appreciative of the times where you go into a situation where your role might be a little bit less, but you’re winning,” Simons said. “That’s something you can’t take for granted.”

stories.title: Embiid and James listed as questionable for Sixers vs. Raptors
stories.summary: The Sixers listed both Joel Embiid and LeBron James as questionable for their game against the Raptors.
stories.detailText: Embiid and James listed as questionable for Sixers vs. Raptors originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers listed both Joel Embiid and LeBron James as questionable for their Thursday night game vs. the Raptors. As has been the case on previous early-season injury reports, James’ official listing was “low back/sciatica management” and Embiid’s was “right foot plantar fascia injury management.” While Thursday’s contest isn’t part of a back-to-back, it’s the sort of situation in which the Sixers have load management matters in mind for the 32-year-old Embiid and 41-year-old James. They’ll host the Pacers on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET and then visit the Nets the following night. James logged 29 minutes Tuesday in the 9-3 Sixers’ loss to the Celtics and Embiid went 31. Embiid said postgame that he rolled his ankle late in the second quarter, but he was fine to play the second half. With the Raptors facing Boston on Wednesday night, Toronto’s complete injury report won’t be available until Thursday afternoon. The Raptors announced Tuesday that superstar Kawhi Leonard will be sidelined for at least one more week because of his left knee injury. Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear) will all remain out for the Sixers against the Raptors.

stories.title: Observations after Sixers shake off slow start, Embiid injury scare to win
stories.summary: The Sixers brushed off their blowout loss to the Celtics and got back in the win column Thursday night.
stories.detailText: Observations after Sixers shake off slow start, Embiid injury scare to win originally appeared on NBC Sports Philadelphia The Sixers brushed off their blowout loss to the Celtics and got back in the win column Thursday night. They overcame a first-quarter deficit as high as 17 points and earned a 123-112 home win over the Raptors. The Sixers moved to 10-3 and Toronto fell to 5-7. Tyrese Maxey had 27 points and eight assists. Joel Embiid added 20 points. Jaylen Brown tallied 18 points and six rebounds. VJ Edgecombe posted 15 points, eight rebounds and a season-high eight assists. Anfernee Simons scored 17 points and shot 5 for 6 from three-point range. RJ Barrett recorded 31 points and 14 rebounds. Immanuel Quickley had 26 points and six assists. The Sixers were without LeBron James (low back/sciatica management), Adem Bona (cervical spine sprain), Dominick Barlow (lower back stress reaction) and Ariel Hukporti (right Achilles tendon tear). The team told reporters Thursday morning that Bona will be re-evaluated in approximately one week and that Barlow participated in shootaround. The 23-year-old forward also went through a pregame workout on the Xfinity Mobile Arena floor. There’s no formal timetable for his return. Toronto’s sidelined players included Kawhi Leonard and Scottie Barnes. The Sixers will face the Pacers on Sunday afternoon in Philadelphia. Here are observations on their victory over the Raptors: Embiid exits early but returns to action Dean Wade began the game in James’ normal spot. The Sixers started slowly, missing their first foul field goals and opening 1 for 8 from three-point range. Embiid had an early injury scare. He stayed down after setting a ball screen and having an apparent knee-to-knee collision with Ja’Kobe Walter. The Sixers called timeout with 8:30 left in the first quarter and Embiid grabbed at his right knee. He eventually rose with assistance from teammates and Sixers head athletic trainer Kevin Johnson, then limped back to the locker room. Jabari Walker entered. At the 5:26 mark of the first quarter, Embiid checked back in to cheers from the home fans. “I knew that he didn’t twist it or anything,” Maxey said. “I knew it was a knee-to-knee, so I wasn’t too worried. He kept saying, ‘I just got kneed.’ That still hurts, though.” Embiid ended up logging 28 minutes, though he certainly wanted to play more. “He was very, very motivated to play,” Sixers head coach Nick Nurse said. “It was hard to get him out for his scheduled rests tonight, which is a good problem sometimes.” While Embiid’s return was a major positive development, the Sixers fell further behind. The Raptors’ lead swelled to 32-16 with a Jamison Battle three-pointer and Nurse burned a timeout. Brown-Edgecombe pair strong in 2nd quarter Simons sunk a buzzer-beating three to conclude the first quarter, cutting the Sixers’ deficit to nine points. “Those are big momentum plays that usually have some weight to them and carry you into the next moment,” Nurse said. The Sixers kept rolling against a shorthanded Toronto team playing on the second night of a back-to-back. Simons nailed a triple to kick off the scoring in the second quarter. Brown buried a mid-range jumper and Edgecombe jammed in a crowd-pleasing dunk to give the Sixers a 35-34 edge. Brown and Edgecombe shined in the second quarter both as individuals and as a duo. The Sixers need Edgecombe to attack a bit more offensively when he shares the floor with Brown and bench players. It doesn’t hurt for the second-year guard to have that clarity about his role in those units. “He’s one of our better playmakers,” Maxey said of Edgecombe. “He’s really good at getting downhill and creating for himself and others.” The Sixers’ only three bench rotation players were Walker, Simons and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope (11 points, five assists). In addition to Walker, Wade got center minutes behind Embiid. Maxey, Sixers pull away Embiid picked up his third foul with 2:23 left in the second quarter and had to take a seat. The teams were tied at 60 apiece through two periods. The game remained even for much of the third, but Maxey fueled an 11-0 Sixers run late in the quarter. His speed and the Sixers’ collective focus on pushing the pace whenever possible allowed the team to get regular points before Toronto could set its defense. Maxey zoomed in for a layup, then tossed the ball ahead to Brown for an easy bucket. Brown assisted a Simons three. Walker converted a fast-break lay-in and canned a three on the first possession of the fourth quarter. All of a sudden, the Sixers held a 101-87 lead. Brown, Edgecombe and the bench gave the Sixers more good minutes early in the fourth quarter. They sealed the deal without any late drama. And the fans chanting for a Tacko Fall appearance got their wish with a final-minute entrance by the 7-foot-6 center.

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Melissa Majchrzak/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images Ascending star Dylan Harper scored 16 of his team’s last 24 points to help San Antonio (12-2) claim its 12th straight victory and third straight this season over the Jazz. With the game still very much in doubt, Victor Wembanyama hit a fadeaway jumper and blocked a Keyonte George floater, and Keldon Johnson saved the ensuing carom from falling out of bounds and chased down an offensive rebound at the other end and scored a putback to put the Spurs up four in the penultimate seconds. In a game with an exasperating amount of runs that were often one after another, Utah staged a 19-7 run spanning hte third and fourth quarters to erase the Spurs’ biggest lead of the night (9) and get into the driver’s seat until the visitors made that final 24-13 push. Harper (31 points, 9 assists, and 4 assists) single-handedly willed San Antonio to victory with audacious and self-assured shotmaking throughout those critical fourth quarter minutes. Wembanyama (23 points, 9 rebounds, 5 assists, and 4 blocks) carried the offenisve production throughout the first three quarters. Stephon Castle (20 points, 9 assists, and 4 steals) and reserve Jordan McLaughlin (10 points) assured Fox wouldn’t be missed TOO much. Johnson (11 points and 10 rebounds) was a menacing presence for the Spurs in the second half and especially in the waning moments. Mo Bamba (26 points [6-for-6 from three], 5 rebounds, and 4 assists) performed admirably again in the absence of the star-studded Jazz starting bigs. Backup Brice Sensabaugh (14 points and 7 rebounds) and rookie Darryn Peterson (17 points, 5 rebounds, and 4 assists) led a group of contributors that supplied plentiful support for Bamba and made up for an off-night for Keyonte George (13 points, 8 assists, and 4 rebounds). The teams mirrored each other over the opening minutes – with Wembanyama and Bamba taking center stage before Rutgers’ Harper and Bailey exchanged buckets. While the bigs’ turned away several shots at or near the rim, the Jazz swingmen made a flurry of threes to get themselves out front. Despite those outside bursts, the Spurs stayed neck-and-neck with their counterparts. While the hosts shot an astounding 7-for-10 fron behind the line, they still only went to the second up two, after McLaughlin kickstarted a closing 8-0 run to end the first quarter. Bamba’s third and fourth threes (without a miss) created some space between his team and San Antonio. While the teams continued to shoot well from the field, Utah’s proficiency from distance made up the bulk of their advantage. After opposing 9-0 runs, the Jazz took advantage of San Antonio’s errant shooting to leap back into the lead. Utah’s perimeter men seemed to make quite a few shots late in the clock. Wembanyama rescued a handful of possessions with his shooting and playmaking and the Spurs went to halftime slightly up 58-55. Coming out of the break, Castle figured in one each of the Spurs’ first four scores – two field goals, two freebies, and one assist. Rookie Peterson dazzled with his ability to score from different spots on the floor. Bamba and Bradley resembled Utah legend Thurl Bailey by knocking down shot after shot. A 10-0 run by San Antonio got them to 79-70. Bamba’s fifth straight three without a miss tied things right back at 79. San Antonio nearly went the rest of the quarter without scoring again and the teams were deadlocked at 81 going to the final 12 minutes. Observations Game Clinching Play #1 : Everything Harper died from the 8:07 mark of the fourth quarter to the final buzzer. Game Clinching Play #2 : With a four-point lead, Castle received a ‘thank you very much’ steal and threw down an uncontested windmill jam I might be repeating myself, but Bamba continues to look like a very competent veteran out there filling in for Markkanen and Jackson, Jr. The mountain outline on the court is immaculate despite all of the trauma those 90s Jazz teams caused us Spurs fans. Small sample size of Fox’s steady consistency… six first half turnovers in his absence. The in-arena cams during the first timeout showcased a dance contest, and well, I won’t get back those two minutes ever again. On the Jazz broadcast, they brought in former slam dunk champion Jeremy Evans for a lengthy first half interview. #obscure2010splayers Area 51 Sequence of the Game : Though the two hadn’t found each other over many of the first 23 minutes, Castle fed Wembanyama in transition in the final minute of the half to close out the scoring. Sequence of the Game #1 : At the end of a 10-0 run late in the third quarter, Keldon Johnson – after scoring two straight lay-ups at the rim – lofted a high lob to Luke Kornet and the big man gently lowered the ball into the rim to make it 79-70. Sequence of the Game #2 : After a Castle steal early in the fourth quarter, the guard had a 3-on-1 fast break with Wembanyama and Harper on opposing wings and chose the Rutgers second-year man for a lay-up. Game Rundown Bamba and Wembanyama (say their names ten times in a row) matched opening pairs of buckets from the tip. The former Rutgers players – Bailey and Harper – traded field goals after that. However, a trio of Jazz triples put them up six. Over several possessions, Wembanyama had some nice two-man action with Vassell and Jordan McLaughlin to mixed results. After dribbling the ball for nearly 20 seconds, Castle willed home a floater. Sensabaugh, like he seems to always do against San Antonio, knocked down a pair of jumpers in the paint to keep the Jazz ahead. Tony Bradley joined a sextet of Jazz players to knock down threes. McLaughlin sandwiched field goals around a Wembanyama three, and despite the Jazz shooting 57% from the field (64% from three), the Spurs ended the quarter down just 31-33. Bamba’s third straight triple put Utah back up five to start the second. Wembanyana’s catch-and-shoot three knotted things briefly at 38. After weathering nine straight from the Jazz, San Antonio answered right back with nine of their own. The Spurs failed to convert several chances to tie the game or re-take the lead. Wembanyama took his time on the right block and tossed up a bankshot-and-1 over Bamba that would have made Tim Duncan proud. Johnson’s transition three put San Antonio up one. While the Jazz executed well over the bulk of the first half minutes, an Area 51 transition lob slam made it 58-55 Spurs at the break. At the start of the third, Castle followed two quick baskets with a couple of free throws and assisted Harper’s and-1 to briefly get the San Antonio lead to ten. Undeterred, Peterson capped a 10-0 Utah avalanche with a corner three and a floater to tie things at 67. The Spurs, with Johnson’s prominent contributions, generated their own 10-0 run while Wembanyama sat to go up 79-70. San Antonio stayed stuck at 79 and was nearly shut out the rest of the quarter aside from some Castle free throws, and the Jazz pulled even at 81 heading to the fourth. For the Jazz fan’s perspective, please visit SLC Dunk . San Antonio returns home to take on Cade Cunningham and the Detroit Pistons on NBA at 7:00 PM CDT.

teamStories.title: Spurs win 12th straight while sending Jazz to 12th straight loss
teamStories.summary: — Dylan Harper had 31 points and nine rebounds to rally the San Antonio Spurs to a 110-102 victory over the Utah Jazz on Sunday, giving them their 12th straight win, while sending the Jazz to a 12th straight loss.
teamStories.detailText: SALT LAKE CITY -- — Dylan Harper had 31 points and nine rebounds to rally the San Antonio Spurs to a 110-102 victory over the Utah Jazz on Sunday, giving them their 12th straight win, while sending the Jazz to a 12th straight loss. Victor Wembanyama finished with 26 points, 11 rebounds, six assists, and five blocks for the Spurs. Stephon Castle added 20 points and nine assists. Keldon Johnson had 11 points and 10 boards. San Antonio outscored the Jazz 27-5 in fastbreak points. Mo Bamba scored 26 points, while going 6 of 6 from 3-point range, to lead Utah. Darryn Peterson scored 17 points for the Jazz. Keyonte George finished with 13 points and eight assists and Brice Sensabaugh added 14 points and seven rebounds off the bench. San Antonio trailed for much of the fourth quarter until Harper tied it at 100 on back-to-back 3s and then Castle hit a pair of free throws to put the Spurs up 102-100 with 2:30 left. Castle’s steal and dunk with 47.2 seconds remaining capped a 14-4 run and extended San Antonio’s lead to 108-102. Utah scored seven baskets over eight possessions, culminating in Mamba’s step-back 3-pointer, to take a 33-23 lead late in the first quarter. San Antonio erased the deficit before halftime. Castle scored a pair of baskets, then fed Harper for a layup, to put the Spurs up 67-57 early in the third quarter. Peterson scored three baskets, culminating in a pull-up 3, to give the Jazz a brief 70-69 lead in the third quarter. San Antonio followed that with a 10-0 run to go up 79-70. Johnson powered the run with back-to-baskets and assisted an alley-oop dunk from Luke Kornet . Up Next Spurs: Host Detroit on Tuesday. Jazz: At Los Angeles Clippers on Tuesday. ------ See AP’s full NBA coverage here

Veterans of the Game Thread know how we do things around here, but for all you newbies we have a few rules. Our community guidelines apply and basically say be cool, no personal attacks, don’t troll and don’t swear too much. The Spurs are looking to extend their win streak to a dozen on an odd single game road trip to Utah for a Sunday afternoon game. The Spurs have already played the Jazz twice this season (three times, if you count preseason), and will likely finish up the season series this afternoon 1 . The Jazz are 1-12 on the season so far, with their only win being on Game 2 of the season against the Pelicans. Their two best players (Markkannen, Jackson Jr.) are injured, and the best player on the active roster right now might be rookie Darryn Peterson, who can score in bunches but doesn’t play of lot of defense. On paper, this looks like an easy win for the Silver and Black, coming off a 37 point wipeout of the Golden State Warriors on Friday night, who were without the services of their superstar player for the contest. NBA games are played on the court, so a paper advantage only matters if you put the opponent away early. As we learned in the Bulls game earlier this week, this is a team that isn’t always focused to start games, and can let less talented squads gain confidence if they aren’t dedicated to playing with effort from the opening tip. One thing that we also saw in the Bulls game is that the Spurs can get away with only playing one half of good basketball against a bad team and still win going away. While that’s fun to watch for some fans, I kind of prefer the end-to-end blowout of the Warriors’ game. If the team can duplicate that kind of effort, we can watch another fourth quarter of Jordan McLaughlin, Carter Bryant, and Tarris Reed stuffing stats and getting some valuable game reps for most of the fourth quarter. Victor Wembanyama should have a field day against Mo Bamba today, and the Spurs triumvirate of talented backcourt players should have an entertaining matchup against Keyonte George and Peterson. Devin Vassell is likely to have a big game as his speed and elite shotmaking should win out against the Jazz’s porous defense. With a solid effort, the starters can get plenty or rest and will be well rested for Tuesday’s game against the Pistons at the Frost Bank Center. Let’s Go SPURS, and De’Aaron must dominate Darryn. There are two games in the season that will be scheduled once the NBA Cup tournament field is set, and there are some unlikely scenarios that involve another meeting between the Jazz and Spurs. Game Prediction: Darryn Peterson sets a record for shot attempts in a game today, but will be nowhere near the record for made baskets. teamStories.detailText: Before the season, when it was announced that Dylan Harper would join the starting lineup as an addition to the backcourt, rather than replacing De’Aaron Fox or Stephon Castle, it naturally raised some questions. Chief among them was how a lineup of three guards would function. Some fair concerns might be if the group is too small and susceptible to getting picked on defensively, or if it might struggle to find offensive chemistry, the “one ball problem.” However, that hasn’t been the case at all. Overall, the Spurs are first in the league in offensive rating and second in defensive rating (adjusted for strength of schedule per dunksandthrees.com). Looking at the lineup data of just the three guards thus far, they are plus 35 points per 100 possessions (per cleaningtheglass.com), ranking in the 100th percentile. Now it is important to note that this three-man group is actually a four-man group, in all honesty. Among the 298 possessions (garbage time filtered out), all of them feature Victor Wembanyama. In fact, there are only two lineups in total: one with the four previously mentioned plus Devin Vassell, and the other with Julian Champagnie. The argument could be made that the group isn’t succeeding in spite of playing three guards but rather that the success they’ve found is augmented by it. Offensively, Wembanyama’s usage leads not only the team but is among the highest in the league at 33.4 percent. But beyond him, Fox, Castle, and Harper each have a usage around 22 to 26 percent. Through the way they’ve shared responsibilities, they’ve found something that is more than the sum of its parts, and thus has led them to the best offensive rating in the NBA at 118.2 (adjusted for strength of schedule per dunksandthrees.com). Turns out having three ball handlers who can attack, a shooter, and the best player in the world makes for a pretty good strategy. On the other side of the court, the numbers are near perfect as well. They sit only behind Oklahoma City in adjusted defensive rating (108.4). If there is a way to attack the three-guard group, the league hasn’t found it yet, so long as the best defender in the world sits behind them. Coach Mitch Johnson has gotten everyone to buy in, and all of this is reflected in the current win streak (11 games) and their adjusted net rating (+9.8, league best). Both of which are too strong to say this isn’t working.

They booed the Cowboys running onto their own field, and they loudly celebrated a 46-40 San Francisco win. In an entertaining game, the 49ers moved to 8-1, and the Cowboys fell to 4-6. Christian McCaffrey had a career-high 161 receiving yards on four catches, two of them touchdowns, and ran for 62 yards and a touchdown on 13 carries. He is the first player in the Super Bowl era with at least 150 receiving yards, two receiving yards, 50-plus rushing yards and at least one rushing touchdown. The 49ers led 38-19 with 11:26 remaining in the fourth quarter. But George Pickens caught a 5-yard touchdown pass, which was followed by a missed 2-point conversion. Ryan Flournoy's 11-yard score with 3:42 left cut their deficit to 38-32. The 49ers burned only 2:26 on their possession in between, punting after four plays. The 49ers showed the Cowboys who they are, though, when Brock Purdy hit McCaffrey across the middle of the field. Von Miller, who was covering McCaffrey, and his teammates had no chance of catching the running back, who went 66 yards to the end zone. The Cowboys didn't go away quietly, scoring once more on CeeDee Lamb's 1-yard reception. Dak Prescott ran in the 2-point conversion. Dallas tried an onside kick despite having three timeouts. Kaelon Black, who had 11 carries for 53 yards and a touchdown, fumbled on the second-down play. Quinnen Williams forced it, but Black was able to get back on the ball. The 49ers punted, and the Cowboys were left with only 9 seconds and in need of 91 yards and a miracle. They didn't get it. McCaffrey's other touchdowns were a 74-yard reception and a 16-yard run. The 49ers had 584 yards, the third-most the Cowboys have allowed in their history. It was not far from the 49ers' team record of 621. Brock Purdy set a career-high with 389 passing yards and threw three touchdowns, completing 22 of 28 passes. George Kittle had six catches for 74 yards, and new addition Keenan Allen five for 61. Deebo Samuel had three catches for 31 yards and a touchdown and three carries for 78 yards and a touchdown. The Cowboys couldn't keep up, even with 439 yards. Dak Prescott was 30-of-51 for 343 yards with five touchdowns and an interception. Pickens had 11 catches for 145 yards and three touchdowns, and Lamb seven for 72 yards and a touchdown. Flournoy added six catches for 71 yards and a touchdown.

stories.title: Patrick Mahomes stars for Chiefs, strikes early connection with Josh Downs
stories.summary: Even with an elbow injury, Patrick Mahomes was able to have his best performance of the year to lead the Chiefs to a dominant 35-13 win over the Falcons.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA -- Minutes before Sunday's game against the Falcons , Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes said he felt more nervous than usual. He wondered how well he'd perform while still dealing with a small sprain of his right UCL suffered just seven days ago. But even in unusual circumstances -- and even as injuries with other teammates piled up as the game progressed -- Mahomes was able to have his best performance of the year to lead the Chiefs to a dominant 35-13 victory . Mahomes used his talented right arm, while wearing a Hyperice elbow sleeve to reduce inflammation between drives, to throw for a season-high 348 passing yards and five touchdowns. "You don't know until you get out there and that adrenaline starts kicking in," Mahomes said, smiling. "Obviously, it was good enough. We did a great job, [athletic trainer] Julie [Frymyer] and the whole training staff all week of just trying to make sure I was in a great spot to go out there and compete. "I'm sure we'll have some ice on it going back home. We'll continue that same process next week." Mahomes exceled without running back Kenneth Walker III , who missed his first game this season due to a groin injury. Then in the first quarter, tight end Travis Kelce aggravated a right ankle injury (he later returned) and right guard Trey Smith sustained a concussion. But Mahomes was able to incorporate newly acquired receiver Josh Downs . Just before halftime, Mahomes moved up in the pocket and delivered one of his his best intermediate throws, a back-shoulder pass that resulted in an 18-yard touchdown catch for the receiver, who joined the Chiefs on Tuesday via a trade with the Colts . "Pat gave me a chance, and I went up and made a play," Downs said. "I'm excited to keep building off of that. First game and first touchdown, you can't write it better than that. Playing with a guy like him is incredible. Doing anything you can to get open for him and making plays is what I want to do." Downs played just 10 offensive snaps (15.9%), but his production was impressive. He was targeted five times and recorded four receptions for 53 yards and a touchdown on just eight routes. His target rate of 62.5% and his 7.6 yards per route were career highs, according to Next Gen Stats. "It looks like there's a connection there," coach Andy Reid said of Mahomes and Downs. "They worked well today -- and that's on two days of practice. We look forward to incorporating him a little bit more as we go along. That one throw for the touchdown right before the half, that's a trust play and he put it up there. The kid made a great play." The Chiefs then created more separation on the scoreboard because Mahomes unleashed one deep pass after another in the second half. Rookie receiver Cyrus Allen beat cornerback A.J. Terrell Jr. on a stop-and-go route for his first career touchdown, a 39-yarder. It marked the first time Mahomes connected on a deep pass (at least 20 air yards) since Week 4. "I told Pat before this week, 'If I'm [against] man coverage, make sure you throw that to me,'" Allen said. "He believed in me." Mahomes generated his longest completion of the season in the fourth quarter. On a play-action pass, Mahomes realized his first two passing options, rookie running back Emmett Johnson and receiver Jalen Royals , were covered. Then Mahomes noticed second-year receiver Andrew Armstrong was in a one-on-one matchup deep against cornerback C.J. Henderson . The play ended with Armstrong catching his first career touchdown, a 43-yarder. "It was good to see other guys step up and make plays, especially against man coverage," Mahomes said. "You've got to win versus man, and I've got to be able to give them chances. If they're going to play man, we have to prove that we're going to beat it." Armstrong celebrated by tossing the ball in the end zone before his teammates congratulated him. Mahomes, though, made sure to scoop the ball up to give it back to Armstrong for him to keep the souvenir. "Those are the best because that man puts in the work every single day," Mahomes said of Armstrong. "He didn't make the team with the number count, but he got back to the practice squad, practiced hard, got called up, blocks his tail off every single time he's asked to and then he goes out there and makes a big play in a big moment." Just a week ago, in a win over the Jets , Mahomes averaged just 2.8 air yards per attempt, the second lowest in a game in his career, according to Next Gen Stats. Against the Falcons, Mahomes completed 3-of-6 passes where the ball traveled more than 20 air yards for 132 yards and two touchdowns. Sunday was Mahomes' first game with multiple deep TD passes since 2021. "He was slinging it," Reid said of Mahomes. "He really did some nice things. He's a luxury to have and to coach, and he does a heck of a job spreading it around, using all of his receivers. You don't see a whole lot of that around the league. He's a great player."

stories.title: Jets QB Geno Smith suffers ankle injury, replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik
stories.summary: Jets quarterback Geno Smith suffered an ankle injury in the third quarter and was replaced by rookie Cade Klubnik on Sunday at MetLife Stadium.
stories.detailText: EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The New York Jets , mired in a historic offensive funk, have a new concern on their long list: an uncertain quarterback situation. Geno Smith injured his left ankle in the third quarter of the Jets' 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills and left MetLife Stadium on a golf cart Sunday evening after a brief stop in the X-ray room. There were no crutches and no visible walking boot. Coach Aaron Glenn didn't provide an update after the game. The Jets turned to rookie Cade Klubnik , who made his NFL debut after riding the bench for nine weeks. The former Clemson, facing a 17-12 deficit when he entered the game, threw an interception and was sacked three times as the spiraling Jets (2-8) lost their fifth straight. They haven't scored a touchdown in nine quarters, tied for the second-longest drought in the NFL this season and their longest since 2023. "Bad ball. Bad football. Not a recipe to win," wide receiver Garrett Wilson said. Things were so bad for the Jets that they became only the second team this century to lose back-to-back games by at least 17 points despite having four scoring drives in each game. It's like there's an invisible wall at the goal line; they haven't reached the end zone despite 64 plays in opponents' territory over the last two games. "Definitely frustrated," said Glenn, who dropped to 5-22 as the head coach, including 0-9 in the AFC East. Glenn was calm after the game, almost too calm. "It doesn't do me any good to sit here and scream and yell at guys [the media]," he added. "That's not going to win us games." Ordinarily, the Jets would've heard loud boos from their home fans, but it was a pro-Bills crowd. Wilson said he was "confused." When he heard cheers, he thought something positive had occurred. "It was like a road game," he said in a moment of gallows humor. "I like road games." Now the Jets face the prospect of playing without Smith, who had been playing reasonably well until the last two weeks. The Jets play the Los Angeles Chargers (0-8), whose 12-quarter touchdown drought -- the league's longest this season -- was snapped last week. Smith (13-for-21, 148 yards) was injured with 4:26 left in the third quarter, when safety Cole Bishop came free on a third-down blitz. Smith unloaded an incomplete pass and fell backward, his left ankle twisting underneath him. Earlier, Smith missed the first series of the third quarter as he underwent a concussion evaluation during halftime. With 25 seconds left in the first half, he was sandwiched by linebackers Terrel Bernard and TJ Parker , with his helmet hitting the turf. The Jets argued in vain for a roughing-the-passer penalty. "He was kind of scrambling around and stepped up," Bernard said. "I tried to get my pad level low to stay off of that strike zone. I tried to go shoulder to him. I hope he's all right. He came back in the game. But yeah. I hope he's all right." He was -- until the ankle injury. In came Klubnik, a fourth-round pick who hadn't played since the preseason. Klubnik, who led a field-goal drive during Smith's concussion evaluation, didn't fare nearly as well in his return stint. All told, he completed only 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards, throwing an interception on a play in which he was drilled by a blitzer. "This was as tough as it gets for any young quarterback, going against this front that really does a good job of rushing the passer," Glenn said. "But just from the naked eye, I thought he did a pretty good job." Klubnik was the No. 2 quarterback in every game this season but never saw action until Sunday. His teammates and coaches love his moxie. "I've got a lot of belief in myself," he said. "There's been a lot of times throughout my life that nobody else believed in me and I've had to believe in myself. I've always had that mindset." Klubnik wanted a different outcome but said it was "a lot of fun" to get in a game. He received a souvenir from the day: Josh Allen 's jersey. "I've looked up to him for a really long time," Klubnik said. "I appreciate him and love watching him play. Wish I could've gotten the win, though."

stories.title: Mike Tomlin expects 'no jersey swaps' between Steelers, Bengals in AFC North battle
stories.summary: The former Pittsburgh Steelers coach was part of the AFC North rivalry for 19 seasons before joining NBC as an analyst this offseason.
stories.detailText: Mike Tomlin is fired up for Steelers vs. Bengals from a different perspective this year. The former long-time Pittsburgh coach weighed in on the two teams’ AFC North rivalry as a panelist on NBC’s “Football Night In America” ahead of their appearance on the network’s “Sunday Night Football” primetime broadcast. “There’s a nastiness to it,” Tomlin said. “It’s genuine bad blood. There will be no jersey swaps after this one. It’s just the reality of it. But as football purists and lovers of the game, you love to see a genuine rivalry. And this is certainly that.” Required reading: Steelers vs Bengals 'Sunday Night Football' TV info, stream, odds for Week 10 game Tomlin coached in the rivalry for 19 years as Steelers coach and famously presided over the 2015 playoff game between the two sides, where big hits and chaotic on-field altercations played a big part in an 18-16 Steelers victory. He resigned after his team lost to the Houston Texans in January. He soon joined up with NBC and has become one of the faces of the network’s NFL coverage before and after SNF games. This will be the first time his path has intersected with the Steelers, creating an interesting dynamic as he analyzes the team he helped build in recent years. He’ll have his eyes on the Pittsburgh defense, primarily, as it goes against the potent Bengals offense led by quarterback Joe Burrow and receivers Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. “I’m like Bart Scott: I can’t wait,” he said. “I want to see the Steelers rush and pass coverage versus Joe Burrow and Co. I got my popcorn ready.” Tomlin also weighed in on Pittsburgh’s rest advantage. The Steelers are coming off of their bye in Week 9, but the Bengals are coming back from an international journey just last week. They beat the Atlanta Falcons 34-17 in Madrid to tie the Steelers atop the division at 6-2, but now need to navigate a high-stakes matchup on just six days of rest. “Let’s take it from [Bengals coach] Zac Taylor’s perspective,” he said. “You got no control over the schedule, and so you acknowledge that elephant in the room, the challenge that is is, the history, and the you present it to your team as a challenge. Something for them to smile in the face of tonight.” This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Mike Tomlin expects 'no jersey swaps' between Steelers, Bengals in AFC North battle

stories.title: Citing short week, Colts sticking with Daniel Jones at QB despite dreadful start
stories.summary: Colts coach Shane Steichen said the team will stick with Daniel Jones as starter despite a two-interception start that earned him a 2026-worst 1.7 QBR.
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS -- Daniel Jones will remain the Colts ' starting quarterback despite turning in one of the worst passing displays of the 2026 season in Sunday's 24-22 victory over the one-win Miami Dolphins , coach Shane Steichen said. The Colts avoided a fourth-quarter collapse to pull out the win, but Jones finished with a 1.7 QBR, the worst of any starting quarterback this season, according to ESPN Research. He completed just 11 of 22 pass attempts for 108 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. Jones' performance earned him a QBR worse than Minnesota Vikings quarterback Carson Wentz 's 2.3 rating against the Buffalo Bills on "Monday Night Football" last week, when Wentz was 8-of-25 with two interceptions, and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield's 2.3 QBR in a Week 8 game in which he completed no passes. The Colts (3-7) play at the Houston Texans on Thursday night, and the quick turnaround makes a quarterback change difficult, Steichen said. "We're on a short week, so we've got to go," Steichen said. But Steichen has previously resisted the pressure to bench Jones even after previous poor performances. When asked what his standard was for making a quarterback change, Steichen said he is constantly evaluating. "I take everything into account," he said. "I always go back and look at the film and make sure, like, on this play, was it his fault? Was it someone else's fault? I think there's a lot that goes into it. Obviously, the biggest thing is taking care of the football moving forward." Jones has struggled to do that this season, throwing his 11th and 12th interceptions Sunday. His 12 picks lead the NFL. Factoring in his three lost fumbles, Jones has an NFL-high 15 turnovers. The Colts traded receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Tuesday just before the NFL trade deadline, further eroding what was already an underwhelming unit. They now lack a healthy receiver who has been a full-time starter in his career ( Alec Pierce remains on injured reserve with a heel injury). Jones also was contending with a beat-up offensive line. Right tackle Jalen Travis missed the game with a knee injury, and left tackle Bernhard Raimann left with a concussion in the first quarter. But even that doesn't excuse Jones' effort Sunday. In the second half, he completed just 4 of 9 attempts for 21 yards against a defense that was allowing the highest completion rate in the NFL. "We're expected to play well week in, week out, and you've got to do that," Jones said. "That's your job. That's my responsibility to the team. So, I understand what happens when I don't, and I've got to be better."

stories.title: Winners & Losers: Don’t count out the short-handed Rams yet
