stories.title: Amon-Ra St. Brown talks lederhosen, Lions' 'human centipede' celebration
stories.summary: Inspired by his mother, St. Brown paired a memorable performance with a coordinated Bavarian look alongside his Lions teammates.
stories.detailText: Detroit Lions receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown set off the German gameday tunnel walk sporting traditional Bavarian attire: a lederhosen and a Bavarian jacket and hat in a return to his mother's homeland. St. Brown was joined by Lions receiver Isaac TeSlaa and long snapper Hogan Hatten , and the group carried beer mugs and offered a toast as they walked out prior to their 35-10 blowout win over New England Patriots on Sunday in Munich. Asked after the game about the fit, St. Brown smiled while saying his mother suggested the look and told reporters, "I'm not going to put on some Amazon lederhosen." St. Brown's mother was born in Leverkusen, and he spent a significant amount of his childhood living in Germany. St. Brown scored two touchdowns Sunday and called his first score "one of the most memorable" of his career. The Lions added a memorable celebration following his second score to mark the occasion. St. Brown said the "human centipede" celebration originated with Lions passing game coordinator Mike Kafka, who showed them an NFL Europe highlight as part of a pregame meeting. The NFL Europe players did the human centipede celebration after scoring a touchdown, and the Lions' skill players loved it. "We were all laughing in the meeting room and said we've got to do it. I said first touchdown we got to do it," St. Brown said. "I scored the first TD, and I was too lit. I forgot to do it. So that was that. ... When I scored [my] second TD, I said now we need to do it. I was on the ground when they pushed me. I said TeSlaa, let's do the celebration. We all did it. It was lit." Major love to St. Brown and the Lions for embracing the local culture in the NFL's second-to-last international game of the season.

stories.title: Kirk Cousins emotional after win in Vikings return, reflects on 'tough 3 years'
stories.summary: Kirk Cousins was emotional discussing his return to the Vikings after their victory over the Packers.
stories.detailText: GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Kirk Cousins managed to hold back tears Sunday morning when he arrived at Lambeau Field. He didn't even try on the way out. After the Minnesota Vikings ' 30-10 victory over the Green Bay Packers , Cousins' first game since the Vikings reacquired him at Tuesday's trade deadline, Cousins let it all out. "It was emotional coming to the stadium," Cousins told ESPN's Lindsey Thiry, his voice catching several times before he headed into the locker room. "Three years ago, tearing my Achilles here. It's been a tough three years. I was just grateful for the opportunity to play here today, and grateful for my teammates and what they did to make this outcome possible." Cousins' six-season tenure as the Vikings' quarterback effectively ended Oct. 29, 2023, when he tore his right Achilles tendon during a 24-10 victory over the Packers. He signed that offseason with the Atlanta Falcons , only to see the Falcons use the No. 8 pick of the 2024 draft on quarterback Michael Penix Jr. After two years in limbo, Cousins signed last spring with the Las Vegas Raiders , who then selected quarterback Fernando Mendoza with the No. 1 pick. The Vikings, however, needed him to do nothing short of rescuing their season when they traded a 2027 third-round pick Tuesday to bring him back. Week 1 starter Kyler Murray is nursing a strained hamstring, and in Week 9, backup Carson Wentz had the worst outing by QBR of any NFL quarterback in a game this season. The Vikings had lost consecutive games after a 6-0 start. On Sunday, Cousins became the first quarterback since at least 1950, when the NFL began tracking quarterback snaps, to start games for different teams in consecutive weeks. He completed 21 of 31 passes for 207 yards and two touchdowns, including a season-high nine completions to receiver Justin Jefferson , and was particularly effective in critical moments of the NFC North matchup. Cousins completed all eight pass attempts during a fourth-quarter drive that gave the Vikings a three-score lead. On third downs, he completed 9 of 12 passes for 110 yards and seven first-down conversions. Jefferson said afterward that with a defense that is playing as well as the Vikings' -- it sacked Packers quarterback Jordan Love eight times and forced four turnovers -- the Vikings' offense needs only to be "mediocre" to do its part." "He did what we needed him to do," Jefferson said, "and that was just pitch and catch, just kind of getting it to the open guys and just letting them be the playmakers. It wasn't really too much of big shots down the field, but it was just dumping it off and getting those extra 3, 4 yards after the catch. So it was definitely great for us. And his composure, his confidence in the huddle, all of that, it definitely created a positive vibe in the huddle." Cousins arrived in Minnesota on Tuesday night, attended his first meeting Wednesday morning and participated in two practices Thursday and Friday. Right tackle Brian O'Neill said the Vikings changed most of their cadences to accommodate Cousins' preferences during the short week, and Cousins said that on a couple of occasions he let coach Kevin O'Connell know what playcalls he was most and least comfortable with. "He's always been mature," O'Connell said. "He's always been meticulous in his preparation. He's always done everything in his power to prepare himself for games. But there was a level of poise. It never felt like at any point from the time we talked on the phone [before the trade] all the way through to giving him a game ball today, where it was anything other than just rock solid, consistent." Said O'Neill: "I can't say enough about what he did all week to prepare. I mean, he has been gone for a couple years, learned a language in Atlanta, learned a language in Vegas, and then in three days switched back to the language we talk about here. And he was running the show and he was in command. It was so awesome to see that. ... [and] a little bit of full circle to have a good feeling again in this locker room, but we got a lot of work to do and we'll keep going." O'Neill was referencing the morose atmosphere in the visitors locker room after their game at Lambeau in 2023, knowing that Cousins would be lost for the season. The Vikings tiptoed around that coincidence this week, and O'Connell said he knew Cousins well enough to avoid the topic entirely. "Kirk's not really wired like that," O'Connell said. Cousins, however, had clearly thought about it himself. "There's so much football up ahead," Cousins said, "but certainly it's gratifying to be able to come back here with the purple on. I think to come back here with another team isn't quite the same. To come back here with the purple on, similar time of year, three years later, it's a blessing, to be able to have a win like we had today. "But there's just so much football ahead, and the story is going to get written much later."

stories.title: QB Jordan Love, Packers frustrated after blowout loss at home to Vikings
stories.summary: Jordan Love and the Packers expressed their frustration after a 30-10 loss to the Vikings.
stories.detailText: GREEN BAY, Wis. -- The Green Bay Packers thought they had their issues protecting Jordan Love figured out. They thought wrong. Just like in the season-opening loss to the Minnesota Vikings , the Packers quarterback was hit, pressured and sacked from all directions Sunday. The only difference was they didn't blow a double-digit lead this time. This one, a 30-10 "butt whuppin" -- as coach Matt LaFleur called it -- was over from the moment the Packers showed they couldn't protect their quarterback. "Definitely frustrated," Love said. "Everyone in that locker room is frustrated." Love was sacked eight times, tied for the most in a game by a Packers quarterback in the last 40 years. Love was pressured on 60% of his dropbacks (21-of-35), a career high, according to ESPN Analytics. Three times in his career, Love has been pressured on at least half of his dropbacks. All three times came this season. Two of those came against the Vikings, who got to Love 50% of the time in Week 1. And just like in the opener, the Vikings went blitz crazy. Love was blitzed on 66% of his dropbacks on Sunday, the third-highest rate of his career. In Week 1, it was 72%, the highest of his career. It left the Packers unable to come up with answers for what Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores keeps throwing at them, and worse yet it left them in last place in the NFC North despite still having a winning record (6-4). "You have a game like that, where it just feels like we're not able to overcome, we're not able to play our game and do things that obviously in previous weeks we've been able to do," Love said. "So definitely frustrated, but it's one of those things we've got to look at it. We've got to see where we can improve." The Packers can start with the offensive line, where they juggled things again. Two weeks after left guard Aaron Banks returned to the starting lineup, the $77 million free agent signing last year was on the bench because the Packers thought street free agent Laken Tomlinson was a better option at left guard, and Banks couldn't beat out Travis Glover at right guard after a week of competition in practice. Meanwhile, on the opening drive of the third quarter, fill-in center John Williams sent a snap sailing wide left and over the head of Love on a shotgun snap for a fumble that the Vikings recovered, one of four Packers turnovers on the day. "We knew they were going to give us pressure pretty much the whole game, and that's what they did," Williams said. "So we need to be better sticking to our game plan, doing the stuff we're coached to do." The Packers finished with a pass block win rate of just 19%, according to ESPN Analytics/NFL Next Gen Stats, meaning they sustained their blocks for at least 2.5 seconds just 19% of the time. It was the Packers' third game with a PBWR under 20%, with two of them coming against the Vikings. All other teams in the NFL have combined for three such games this season. When asked how frustrated Love was with the lack of protection, LaFleur said, "I think we're all frustrated." That F-word was the catchphrase of the day in the losing locker room. "I was frustrated myself," said receiver Christian Watson , who had three catches for 37 yards. "But I wasn't thinking about [Love] in that aspect too much or seeing that from him. But I wouldn't put it past him to be frustrated." The Packers were coming off perhaps their best game of the season, a 45-27 win over the New England Patriots in which Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns while getting hit just five times. He took 12 hits Sunday after the Vikings clobbered him 15 times in the opener. At one point in the third quarter, Love was slow to get up after taking a hit and reached for his lower back. By late in the fourth quarter, LaFleur had seen enough of his quarterback getting battered and took him out with 3:56 left in the game. "I'm all right," Love said. "Took some shots, for sure. "There was one I just got stepped on pretty good," Love added. "I was just kind of bruised, tried to get back up from that, but I'll be fine."

stories.title: 9 Winners and 3 Losers from the Chiefs’ win over the Falcons
stories.summary: Here are the names that stood out from Kansas City’s victory over Atlanta.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Your Kansas City Chiefs kept pace in the AFC race by outclassing the Atlanta Falcons from kickoff to the final play. Somehow, the game wasn’t even as close as the 35-13 score would indicate. The new-look, next-man-up Chiefs offense had its way with the Falcons defense on the ground and in the air. Meanwhile, the Chiefs defense stifled a talented Atlanta offense, keeping them from sniffing the end zone until the fourth quarter. Here are a few who stood out on Sunday — more good than bad this time. 9 Winners Wide receiver Josh Downs: Any questions about why the Chiefs went out and traded for Josh Downs? Anyone? In limited snaps, No. 12 quickly became a favorite target for Patrick Mahomes. Downs caught 4 of 5 targets for 51 yards and a spectacular touchdown. Earning Mahomes’ trust for a back-shoulder throw in the end zone is a big deal. The way Downs helped open up the entire offense is even bigger. He also handled (and mishandled) punt returns in a really solid Chiefs debut. Running back Emmett Johnson: The Chiefs went out this offseason and brought in two #1 running backs. In his first career start, the rookie went off — 22 carries, 6 catches for 171 total yards and two receiving touchdowns. The unfortunate injury to Ken Walker should be healing well while he watches the kid dominate for another week if needed. Defensive ends George Karlaftis and Ashton Gillotte: These two picked up right where they left off last week. Both were too much for the Atlanta offensive line and made Michael Penix Jr.’s afternoon miserable. Karlaftis had 1.5 sacks and another batted pass, while Gillotte notched two tackles-for-loss a sack and a batted pass of his own. Steve Spagnuolo and Joe Cullen seem to be building a rotation of diverse skill sets on defense, getting production from these guys and solid play from Felix Anudike-Uzomah and Khyiris Tonga. Linebackers Drue Tranquill and Nick Bolton: Remarkably, the pass-rush success came while they held the NFL’s best running back to 71 yards on the afternoon. Substantial credit goes to the duo of Bolton and Tranquill, who combined for 18 total tackles (one for a loss). Their aggressive tackling helped contain Bijan Robinson and kept the Falcons offense from sustaining drives. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes: It wasn’t just the numbers, although they were spectacular— 348/5/0. It was the confident downfield throws to a number of different targets. It was the stepping up in the pocket, the scrambles and the tight spirals. It was a vintage Patrick Mahomes game, the likes of which we haven’t seen in a while. He threw a touchdown after a penalty erased a Chiefs field goal. He threw a deep touchdown when the Falcons took away the short option he wanted. He gave his receivers a chance to make a play—and they delivered this week. Wide receivers Cyrus Allen and Andrew Armstrong: Both young receivers hauled in their first NFL touchdown this week—39 yards for Allen, 43 for Armstrong. Cyrus Allen showed off his route running— using a double move to blow by the cornerback for a wide-open score. Andrew Armstrong made a great adjustment to a ridiculous throw by an improvising Patrick Mahomes. When the quarterback shows this much trust in his receivers, especially ones he hasn’t played with as much— the league is in trouble. Honorable mention : Rashee Rice, who caught a 50-yard bomb this week and led the team, bringing in 5/6 targets for a team-high 82 yards. 3 Losers Wide receiver Xavier Worthy: Not every receiver was able to feast on Sunday. Worthy caught exactly none of his three targets and seemed to get out-hustled on a successful Falcons onside kick. The offense worked well without a contribution from Worthy, which doesn’t bode well for his value going forward. The Chiefs’ depth chart: Injuries seem to be piling up— Kelce was in and out with an ankle, Trey Smith had a concussion, Jared Wiley hurt an ankle, and Creed Humphrey went out for a while after being poked in the eye. The Chiefs were already thin on offense with Ken Walker and Jaylon Moore out. When Mike Calliendo, Hunter Norzad, and Nate Carter are in the game, things don’t usually go this well. Special teams coach Dave Toub: On one hand, Harrison Butker didn’t miss a kick for once. On the other hand, the Chiefs’ special teams units still made the kinds of mistakes that led us to question their leadership. After cutting Nikko Remigio (likely the right move), Toub tried a few returners, including newly signed Josh Downs, who fumbled and recovered his first punt return. The coverage units missed more tackles than usual, and there were still costly penalties on special teams. This group feels like a bit of a mess. Note: Applying the labels “winners” or “losers” is not meant to be a judgment on the talent or character of any of these individuals. It’s just a simple way to grade their job performance in a single game. No disrespect is intended.

stories.title: Sean McVay showcases his ability to adapt in Rams' blowout win over Cardinals
stories.summary: With his top receivers out, Sean McVay utilizes Blake Corum and Kyren Williams at the same time and deploys other changes in the Rams' 34-6 victory.
stories.detailText: Rams safety Kamren Kinchens (5) celebrates with his teammates after intercepting a pass in the second quarter of a 34-6 win over the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday at State Farm Stadium. (Mike Christy / Getty Images) Sean McVay knows how to artfully pivot. And not just when he wants to sidestep answering a question. No, the Rams ’ coach showed last season that he could change directions — and formations — on a dime when he switched to a tight-end heavy set that helped the Rams’ offense flourish into the NFL’s most productive unit. On Sunday, with star receivers Davante Adams and Puka Nacua on injured reserve, the resourceful McVay masterfully did it again. He deployed running backs Kyren Williams and Blake Corum at the same time. He utilized an extra offensive lineman on occasion. And he survived two centers leaving the game because of injuries as the Rams routed the Arizona Cardinals 34-6 at State Farm Stadium. Read more: With NFL's toughest schedule looming, Rams quiet at trade deadline as rivals make deals Matthew Stafford passed for three touchdowns and Corum rushed for 100 yards and scored a touchdown as the Rams extended their winning streak to four games. Kam Kinchens and Wesley Bailey intercepted passes and the Rams amassed five sacks as they improved to 6-4 heading into a bye, something McVay and his charges have been looking forward to for weeks. The Rams do not play again until the night before Thanksgiving, when they will host the Green Bay Packers in a game that could have huge playoff implications. Every team in the NFC North is in playoff contention. The Detroit Lions (7-2), Chicago Bears (7-2), Minnesota Vikings (7-2), and the Packers (6-4) are fighting for the division title and wild-card spots. The San Francisco 49ers (7-1), defending Super Bowl-champion Seattle Seahawks (6-4) and the Rams are contending in the NFC West. With only one team from the NFC East and NFL South on track for the playoffs, the wild-card teams that get in — and are left out of the playoffs — will come from the North and West. Rams running back Blake Corum carries the ball against the Arizona Cardinals in the first half Sunday. (Ross D. Franklin / Associated Press) The Rams have what ESPN last week ranked as the toughest remaining schedule, with games against the Packers, Kansas City Chiefs, at the 49ers, Dallas Cowboys, and two games against the Seahawks sandwiched around a trip to Tampa Bay. Sunday’s victory over the Cardinals gave the Rams a chance to breathe a sigh of relief going into a break that could enable players such as Adams, tight end Terrance Ferguson and defensive lineman Kobie Turner to heal — and for edge rusher Myles Garrett to continue getting into a rhythm. But along with McVay’s resourcefulness, the Rams showed against the Cardinals that they have depth. Stafford completed passes to nine receivers. Konata Mumpfield, Tutu Atwell, Xavier Smith and rookie CJ Daniels all had receptions of more than 20 yards in the first half. Smith, who was released by the Rams in October and signed off the San Francisco 49ers’ practice squad last week, caught a touchdown pass at the end of the first half. In Week 6, the Cardinals defeated the Rams 18-16 at SoFi Stadium despite not scoring a touchdown. On Sunday, in rookie quarterback Carson Beck’s first NFL game for the Cardinals, the Rams once again only gave up field goals, and this time they created turnovers and had more than enough offense to keep the Cardinals winless at home since Week 2 of the 2025 season. Read more: 'I am that closer.' Myles Garrett's three-sack performance shows why Rams traded for him The Rams took control late in the first half by scoring two touchdowns in less than a minute. First, Stafford capped a drive with a short touchdown pass to tight end Tyler Higbee with 1:06 left in the second quarter for a 10-6 lead. On the ensuing series, Cardinals receiver Devin Duvernay dove for a pass, but as he rolled on the turf the ball popped into the air and into the hands of Kinchens, who returned it 33 yards. Stafford then found Smith over the middle for a 22-yard touchdown. Corum’s short touchdown run early in the third quarter started the rout and Stafford’s touchdown pass to tight end Davis Allen increased the lead to 31-6. Corum finished with 100 yards in 17 carries and caught three passes for 19 yards. Williams rushed for 23 yards in 12 carries and caught two passes for nine yards. It wasn’t all good news: Center Coleman Shelton left the game in the second quarter because of a hamstring injury and was replaced by Dylan McMahon. McMahon soon after suffered a knee injury and was replaced by Beaux Limmer. Rams players will be off for nearly a week before beginning preparations for the Packers. But McVay will be busy planning his next moves. Get the best, most interesting and strangest stories of the day from the L.A. sports scene and beyond from our newsletter The Sports Report. This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

stories.title: Emmett Johnson proves a lot to Chiefs in 100-rushing yard game
stories.summary: Kansas City learned that its backfield still has high-quality talent when its lead back is out.
stories.detailText: (Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images) When news broke on Friday that the Kansas City Chiefs ’ starting running back Kenneth Walker (groin) would be questionable for Sunday, there was some concern about the sudden injury and its affect on this game, a potentially tricky road spot. However, many in Chiefs Kingdom — including a passionate faction in Lincoln, Nebraska — turned their attention to rookie running back Emmett Johnson. In Week 10, against the Atlanta Falcons , he made his first career start after Walker was ruled out, and he delivered on the anticipation for a heavy workload. Johnson started strong with 48 total yards on the opening drive and finished with 171 yards from scrimmage, looking every bit the part of a starting running back. According to NFL Next Gen Stats , Johnson forced 10 missed tackles on the way to 100 rushing yards. He has the highest rate of missed tackles forced (46%) among running backs with at least 50 touches this year; his teammate, Walker, sits at third on that list. It speaks to the lack of drop-off from the Chiefs’ offense overall, especially the run game. Johnson had a special performance, and head coach Andy Reid made sure it was as memorable as possible by ensuring he passed the century mark. “Emmett, getting himself over 100 yards there with the help of the offensive line, I thought that was great,” Reid told reporters at the podium after the win. “We left him in there so we could get that, and he took care of business there.” Johnson’s big game happened despite multiple injuries up front. Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) was ruled out before the game, then right guard Trey Smith entered concussion protocol in the first quarter. Still, the offense found a rhythm by riding Johnson. The playmaking was evident to everyone involved. “I look at the players; the players have confidence in him, and the players are going to tell you the whole story,” Reid pointed out. “He’s doing the right things, as far as protections go, the cerebral part of the game, he’s taking care of that part. Knowing the plays, the direction of the plays, how to set the plays, all those things, he’s got — and then he has that skill that goes with it. He wants to be in there; he’s a great kid that way.” Johnson helped the Chiefs continue to build on the early lead he earned with a third-down catch and run into the end zone. By the fourth quarter, his attention had turned to ball security, helping Kansas City ice the game away. It’s a veteran detail for the rookie back, something Reid made sure to point out about Johnson. He talked about the Falcons forcing four turnovers in an upset of the San Francisco 49ers earlier this season, and how the rookie noted the performance. “Emmett, more so than any of us, was aware of that,” Reid said about the Falcons’ takeaway potential. “He saw it on tape. Keeping the ball high and tight becomes important; covering it in traffic, he did all of those little things. If you’re going to spin, keep it close to your body. All of the little fundamental things, I think he did a nice job with. We all have trust in him, he does that, he’s very coachable and a smart kid.” The trust that Johnson has built, from his teammates to the coaching staff, will only become more important as the season wears on. Walker won’t be 100% all the time, so even when he isn’t, the Chiefs still have a high-quality back to keep the offense on track.

stories.title: NFC North will either make NFL history or cannibalize itself | Opinion
stories.summary: NFC North teams have lost a combined 10 games this season, and all but four have been to division foes.
stories.detailText: The Black and Blue Division is back in glorious fashion. Well, glorious for everyone outside the NFC North potentially. The entire NFC playoff field, including the No. 1 seed, is likely going to come down to whether or not the NFC North continues to eat its own in the second half of this NFL season. There is little question the NFC North is the NFL’s best division this season. Maybe ever, as it threatens to end the NFL’s streak of no division ever having all four teams in the playoffs. Three of the NFC North’s teams — the Detroit Lions , the Minnesota Vikings and the Chicago Bears — are comfortably in the postseason mix at 7-2 each. The Green Bay Packers are still in contention for that last wild-card spot despite dropping to 6-4 with a 30-10 loss to the Vikings on Sunday, Nov. 15. The division is so strong that Green Bay, NFC North cellar dweller that it is, would lead both the NFC East and the NFC South . The only thing standing between the NFC North and that historical finish is itself. NFC North toughest on its own Of the 10 combined losses the NFC North teams currently have, only four were to a non-division opponent. Three of Green Bay’s four losses were to fellow NFC Northers. Both of Chicago’s were. The NFC North beats up on each other so badly the Lions are the only team yet to lose to a division opponent. And there’s more carnage to come! Much, much more. There are six games between NFC North teams the rest of the season, and all but one is Week 15 or later. The Lions, who currently lead the division, and Bears have four games left against division foes. The Vikings and Packers each have two more. All of which means the NFC North standings could look a lot different come early January. So, too, the NFC playoff race. “There’s a lot of football in front of us. Seven more guaranteed games,” Packers coach Matt LaFleur said after Sunday's game. “It’s one week at a time. … There’s a lot to learn from in this game when you get whooped like that. You’ve got to regroup and stay together.” No common thread to NFC North dominance What makes the NFC North’s dominance so appealing is the teams are very different. Different than what the NFC North has been historically, too. This is not a division that just lines up and runs the ball down your throat for four quarters. The Lions have the NFC’s most prolific offense, and don’t beat themselves with turnovers. The Bears have irrational confidence, never believing they’re out of a game and, more often than not, finding a way to prove themselves right. The Packers have arguably the best wide receiving tandem in Christian Watson and Matthew Golden, and could be diabolical if they got a run game or an offensive line that could block somebody. Anybody. The return of Kirk Cousins gives the Vikings a serviceable offense, which might be enough when they have the nastiest defense in the NFL. Minnesota has allowed all of 126 points through nine games. “With this defense, I think we’re going to have a chance. They’re going to keep us in games and then we’ve got to go make plays when it counts,” Cousins said on Sunday in his postgame interview with Fox. “It’s going to be a grind, but I think with this defense we’re always going to have a chance.” Familiarity breeds ... good football teams Though the NFC North teams are all different, there is one thing they have in common: Familiarity. All the NFC North coaches except Ben Johnson of the Bears have been with their teams five years or longer, and Johnson was on Detroit's staff for six years before coming to Chicago last season. Now that Cousins is back, every starting quarterback has been in the division for at least three seasons. That longevity, combined with playing each other twice each season, gives the NFC North a backyard brawl-like atmosphere. These teams know each other as well as they know themselves. Their tendencies. Their strengths and weaknesses. Their fan bases don't like each other and sometimes the coaches don't , either. It makes for high-adrenaline, high-intensity chess matches. Of course those games against non-division foes are going to seem easy by comparison, and the records reflect it. Every NFC North team could be dangerous in the postseason. So long as they survive their own division first. Follow USA TODAY Sports columnist Nancy Armour on social media @nrarmour. stories.title: Carson Beck starts off strong, then the Arizona Cardinals get blown out by Los Angeles Rams
stories.summary: Arizona Cardinals lose 34-6 to Los Angeles Rams.
stories.detailText: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - NOVEMBER 15: Quarterback Carson Beck #19 of the Arizona Cardinals greets teammate Tyler Allgeier #22 before a game against the Los Angeles Rams at State Farm Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Mike Christy/Getty Images) | Getty Images It did not start too bad for Carson Beck. In the Arizona Cardinals rookies first two drives he lead the team to two field goals. Beck was 3/3 for 34 yards 2-3 for 35 yards So, in two scoring drives Beck was 5/6 for 69 yards. After that Beck was 6/12 for 39 yards, two interceptions and a fumble and the Arizona Cardinals did not score again. First off, none of this is on Carson Beck. The second interception, egregious, but he was in a position where he is trying to make a play. However, it was 10-6 and the Cardinals were about 5-7 yards away from kicking a makeable (albeit very long) field goal. Instead, Devin Durvenay causes an interception off a drop, the Rams go down and score and we get a 17-6 game at the half instead of at worst a 10-6 game. From there, it was the flood gates. Rams touchdown drive to make it 24-6. Beck interception… 14 yards on offense. Rams touchdown drive to make it 31-6. Arizona Cardinals go four and out, gain nine yards. Field goal, 34-6. Five play, 13 yards, and a punt!!! At this point, the game is already out of hand, you are down 4 scores, just go for it. Instead, the Rams get the ball back and run 12 minutes and 15 seconds off the clock with former Cardinals great Ronnie Rivers accounting for 81 yards rushing, and ending the game. This was a nightmare… disaster… expected? We are onto the Chiefs… Oh god, we are onto the Chiefs.

stories.title: Rams roll to 34-6 victory over Cardinals
stories.summary: After winning four in a row, Los Angeles heads into a Week 11 bye at 6-4.
stories.detailText: Dealing with numerous injuries on offense, the Rams understandably got off to a slow start in Sunday’s game against the Cardinals. But Los Angeles got going late in the second quarter and went on to roll to a 34-6 blowout victory. The Rams have now won four in a row after starting the season 2-4, with their last loss coming on Oct. 18 to the Cardinals at home. Starting late in the second quarter, the Rams scored four consecutive touchdowns to make the game a laugher. Quarterback Matthew Stafford hit Tyler Higbee with a 5-yard touchdown to get things started with just over a minute left in the second period. Then after a Kam Kinchens interception, Stafford connected with Xavier Smith for a 22-yard touchdown on a screen pass to give L.A. a 17-6 halftime lead. Blake Corum kept the roll going to open the second half, scoring on a 1-yard run. Then Stafford hit Davis Allen for a 19-yard TD to make the score 31-6 with 5:55 left. Brandon McManus closed out the scoring with a 43-yard field goal. The Rams finished the game holding the ball for the final 12:15 of the contest, with Ronnie Rivers getting 81 yards on 15 carries to close it out. L.A. ended the game leading time of possession 42:23 to 17:37. The Rams had 28 first downs, 436 total yards, and were 7-of-12 on third down. Arizona had just six first downs, 123 total yards, and the team was 0-of-6 on third down. Corum led Los Angeles with 100 yards on 17 carries with a touchdown. He also caught three passes for 19 yards. Matthew Stafford was 18-of-26 for 249 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. Making his debut, rookie Carson Beck finished 11-of-18 for 108 yards with two picks. The Rams will now go into their abbreviated Week 11 bye at 6-4. They will next host the Packers on Wednesday of Week 12. Arizona falls to 3-7 on the season. The club will be on the road to face Kansas City next Sunday.

stories.title: Rams vs. Cardinals final score: L.A. wins convincingly in AZ
stories.summary: The Los Angeles Rams win their fourth game in a row, and look great doing it
stories.detailText: The Los Angeles Rams (6-4) put together their finest team win of the year over the Arizona Cardinals (3-7) in Week 10 of the NFL season with a final score of 34-6, and notched their fourth win in a row. The Rams completely choked out the Cardinals and basically had won this game halfway through the third quarter. Sean McVay called a gorgeous closing drive to chew up the fourth quarter and end this game with a decisive win for L.A. With the Rams having lost to the Cardinals earlier in the year, this was a great way to get back on track and build confidence in both the team and fanbase. The Cardinals struck first with a field goal and the Rams offense struggled in the first quarter, but they took a 17-6 lead going into halftime and kept their foot on the gas from there. Matthew Stafford threw a bad interception in the first quarter, but rallied to throw three touchdowns to Tyer Higbee, Xavier Smith (his first career score) and Davis Allen before the final whistle blew. Stafford continues to have uninspiring moments with regard to the turnovers, but he’s still putting up enough numbers to hold the QB1 job as he helped guide the Rams to a dominant win on Sunday. First career INT for @Cody_Simon30 🙂‍↕️ #LARvsAZ on @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/cnQKQoX5JE — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) November 15, 2026 L.A.’s defense held Arizona to two field goals, and made life very hard on rookie quarterback Carson Beck who threw two interceptions, including one before halftime that helped give the Rams a 17-6 lead which then allowed the Rams to take a commanding lead. They only added to it from there as the defense didn’t allow Mike LaFleur and his Cardinals to get in any sort of groove. FIRST NFL TOUCHDOWN FOR XAVIER SMITH!! 🙌 📺 @NFLonCBS | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/ZIhTbMxp7i — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 15, 2026 The ground game for the Rams featured Blake Corum in more of a lead back role, though Kyren Williams still technically started, Corum had 17 carries for 100 yards to Williams’ 23 yards on 12 carries. Corum scored again for his sixth straight game, and by the fourth quarter Ronnie Rivers was filling in for both Corum and Williams to close out the game. Sixth straight game with a Blake Corum touchdown!! 📺 @NFLonCBS | #RamsHouse pic.twitter.com/HlvmMNCVZx — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) November 15, 2026 Was this the most dominant win of the season for the Rams? It seemed that way, as the defense played strong all game, and the offense got it going in the second quarter and didn’t look back. Special teams are still bit of a concern with Joshua Karty gifting 40-yard starting field position to the Cardinals with two kickoff penalties. Though, Brandon McManus was solid as he delivered on each of his kick attempts and remains perfect on the season. This team still has a lot of work to do but in Week 10, the Rams won convincingly over their division rival, and move to 6-4 to keep pace in the crowded NFC and NFC West. Now, the Rams enter their bye week before taking on the Green Bay Packers in Week 12 in a game that should have major playoff implications for both teams. stories.title: Back from Madrid, Bengals face Steelers team that is back from a bye
stories.summary: The Bengals host the Steelers on Sunday night in Week 10.
stories.detailText: The Bengals host the Steelers on Sunday night in Week 10. Their Week 9 experiences couldn't have been more different. The Bengals played the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. The Steelers didn't play anyone; they were on their bye. The end result is that, for the sixth time ever, a team that played internationally will be facing a team that was on a bye. (One of those occasions involved the Bills playing in Toronto, so it's not quite the same.) The teams that were off the week before facing a team that played outside the U.S. have a record of 5-0 in those games. There's another bye-week fact that favors the Steelers. Pittsburgh has won nine games in a row following their bye week, since 2017. Via NBC Sports research, it's the third-longest streak in NFL history, behind only the 1999-2011 Eagles (who won 13 in a row) and the 2015-present Bills (who have won 12 in a row). Of course, those nine straight wins were accomplished by former coach Mike Tomlin. This is current coach Mike McCarthy's first post-bye opportunity. Having it come against a team that played across an ocean last Sunday can't hurt. It happens again next week; the Lions return from Germany to host a Bucs team that was off in Week 10.

stories.title: Badgers grades, snap counts on defense from Week 11 vs. Maryland: Wisconsin had 1 key problem on Saturday
stories.summary: The Badgers defense played well, but it wasn’t enough in the loss.
stories.detailText: COLLEGE PARK, MARYLAND - NOVEMBER 14: Head coach Luke Fickell of the Wisconsin Badgers leads his team onto the field before the game against the Maryland Terrapins at SECU Stadium on November 14, 2026 in College Park, Maryland. (Photo by G Fiume/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Wisconsin Badgers fell in a 24-21 upset to the Maryland Terrapins on Saturday, marking their second straight loss to Maryland, which got its second conference win of the year. It was an inexcusable win and one that the defense played well in for much of the game. But there were a few issues, including a coverage bust and lack of pressure on the quarterback, that proved to be costly in the loss. Here are the PFF grades and snap counts for Wisconsin’s defense in the loss to Maryland. Defensive Line Charles Perkins – Snap Count: [31], Grade: 62.2 Hammond Russell IV – Snap Count: [30], Grade: 57.1 Junior Poyser – Snap Count: [24], Grade: 70.8 Nolan Vils – Snap Count: [23], Grade: 80.8 Micheal Garner – Snap Count: [21], Grade: 64.4 Dillan Johnson – Snap Count: [8], Grade: 51.8 DeNigel Cooper – Snap Count: [5], Grade: 65.2 Jacob Anderson – Snap Count: [3], Grade: 63.1 Wisconsin rotated a ton again on the defensive line. Nolan Vils and Charles Perkins stood out here with three defensive stops each. I thought the Badgers would rely more on some of their jumbo edges like Micheal Garner and Justus Boone without Sebastian Cheeks, and they went in that direction, while spreading the snaps around up front. stories.title: 5-touchdown reminder: Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs are alive and well
stories.summary: Mahomes threw five touchdown passes in a game for the first time since 2022 in blowout victory over the Falcons.
stories.detailText: ATLANTA — He's lurking. While the rest of the NFL universe is falling all over itself praising Josh Allen and Joe Burrow, while everyone's anointing the Chicago Bears and the Jacksonville Jaguars as the new kings of the NFL, Patrick Mahomes is still quietly on the prowl. Or, was . After Sunday's spectacular performance — five touchdowns and 348 yards passing in a 35-13 road win over Atlanta — Mahomes and the Chiefs are flat-out rolling, even with an aging core and an array of new arrivals and rookies. Kansas City missed the playoffs last January after Mahomes was lost for the season, and he's already taken hits this year that have Chiefs fans twitching . Only a handful of starting quarterbacks — guys like Rodgers, Prescott, Cousins, Stafford and Goff — are older than the 31-year-old Mahomes. And yet, when he's slinging it like he did Sunday, it feels like he's never going away, either. "He's a luxury to have and to coach," Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said after the game. "He does an excellent job of spreading around and using all of his receivers. He's not afraid to use any of them. You don't see a lot of that around the league." KC pushed around Denver in Week 1, then beefed up on high-calorie opponents like Indianapolis, Miami, Las Vegas and the Los Angeles Chargers. When Kansas City faced some tougher opposition — Seattle and Denver on the road — the Chiefs folded. Atlanta wouldn't be a playoff-caliber team in any respectable division, but still … you can't argue with five touchdowns to four different receivers, including one who just joined the Chiefs a few days ago. Josh Downs, who arrived in Kansas City via a trade-deadline deal with Indianapolis, took all of a single half to get into rhythm with Mahomes, scoring his first touchdown in a Chiefs uniform with 18 seconds remaining in the first half. "Our new guy, Downs, it looks like there's a connection there, right?" Reid said with a smile. "They worked well today, and that's on two days of practice." "We haven't got a ton of reps, and that's why there's some times you're going to see on tape [from Sunday] where he was open and I didn't give him chances," Mahomes said. "But whenever you do it in the game, that's the best reps to get. I'll be able to have that trust as the season goes on." Patrick Mahomes (15) celebrates after wide receiver Andrew Armstrong (85) caught a touchdown pass during the Chiefs beatdown of the Atlanta Falcons. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Downs finished the day with four receptions, 53 yards and a touchdown. Also in the mix: Cyrus Allen with 44 yards and a touchdown, Andrew Armstrong with 43 yards and also a touchdown, and Rashee Rice with a team-leading 82 yards. Travis Kelce, Mahomes' career-long security blanket, had two catches for 30 yards, separated by a quick trip into the locker room after a hard tackle . "Kells [Kelce] left for a bit with a calf," Reid said. "He's been battling this ankle. … Kind of landed on it that first catch and twisted up a little bit." Reid didn't indicate there was anything more serious with the Chiefs' most tabloid-famous player, and from a football perspective, Mahomes now has the luxury of relying on half a dozen receivers who aren't Travis Kelce. "More than anything, [Sunday] proves that we can attack down the field like we believe that we can," Mahomes said. "If [defenses] are going to come down and try to stop the run, we have to prove that we can throw it down the field. It just showcases another level to our offense that we can continue to get better and better." Here's what makes Kansas City even more dangerous. Mahomes knew he had to shoulder a heavier load than usual Sunday with Kenneth Walker III out with a groin injury. What he probably wasn't expecting, however, was the sudden and explosive emergence of rookie Emmett Johnson, who rushed for 101 yards and hauled in 70 yards' worth of Mahomes passes for two touchdowns on the afternoon. "I'm so happy for him because he comes in with the right mindset every single day. He has a smile on his face, he wants to be great, he wants to contribute in any way possible," Mahomes said. "Obviously, with having Kenneth and how great he's playing, he hasn't got as many opportunities. But when his number got called, he stepped in and made the plays happen. That's going to be great to have as the season goes on and we get Kenneth back as that one-two punch." Part of the hesitation to commit to the Chiefs as a bona fide contender is the status of Mahomes' elbow. He suffered a hit during last week's game against the Jets that had him hanging his arm by his side, although he stayed in the game. ESPN reported Sunday morning that the Chiefs had consulted with elbow specialists from the Kansas City Royals and Texas Rangers, both of whom signed off on Mahomes' Sunday start. "I was a little nervous going into the game just because it was a little sore," he said. "I didn't feel like during the week of practice I was driving the ball the way I wanted [on] some of those deeper in-cut routes and getting the balls down the field. You don't know until you get out there and that adrenaline starts kicking a little bit. Obviously, it was good enough." Two of Mahomes' receivers, Armstrong and Allen, recorded their first career touchdowns on Sunday, a fact that didn't escape Mahomes' attention. "Playing in the NFL is a dream … you never know if you're ever going to get that first touchdown when you get here," he said. "I still know exactly where my first touchdown football is, and I know how important it is to me whenever people come to the house and ask about it." After both touchdowns, Mahomes raced downfield and made sure to secure the footballs for the two rookies. "When you score, you're just celebrating, you're not really paying attention to what's going on," he said. "So I just made sure to grab that so that they have that memory, because they've worked their entire life to be here. They get in the end zone. Not a lot of people get to do that, and so they'll have that for the rest of their life." And they had Patrick Mahomes throw it to them, a fact that becomes more impressive by the year.

stories.title: Buffalo Bills ground New York Jets, improve to 8-1 with Week 10 win
stories.summary: The Buffalo Bills improve to 8-1 on the strength of an unstoppable rushing attack led by James Cook III
stories.detailText: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - NOVEMBER 15: James Cook #4 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball against the New York Jets in the third quarter of a game at MetLife Stadium on November 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Sarah Stier/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills earned their first AFC East divisional win this season thanks to a persistent attack that gradually wore down an overmatched New York Jets team in all three phases of the game. The Bills were once again held in check until halftime, but the offense came out with an aggressive swagger after the break that broke most of the Jets’ prior momentum. You might say that head coach Joe Brady has put together a masterclass in his first season at the helm, lulling opponents into a false sense of hope through the first two quarters, only to pull the rug out from under them when it counts. Buffalo again started the game on offense, thanks to another lost coin toss. It didn’t work out as Brady probably planned for in New Jersey, though the choice wasn’t his to make this weekend. The Jets’ forced a punt that soon ushered in a mid-tempo battle in the trenches for the duration of the half. The Bills eventually found the end zone in the first quarter thanks to another goal-line carry by Allen. The Jets’ defense caused plenty of early confusion and frustration for Allen and the passing game, ultimately holding them to just 10 points at halftime. Thankfully, Buffalo’s defense was ready for a slugfest and limited the Jets to just two field goals through two quarters while having to defend two different quarterbacks in starter Geno Smith (who was injured before the break), and rookie quarterback Cade Klubnik. If you caught his quick interview after the half, it was clear Brady was annoyed at his mostly stagnant first-half offense. They responded to what must have been an epic challenge speech in the locker room, which led to three second-half touchdowns and a 31-12 blowout win. A defense that’s been ranked as low as last and currently resides in the middle of the pack held an under-the-radar and (yes) talented Jets offense out of the end zone. These are the sorts of building blocks that matter when it comes to postseason discussions. The Bills can’t control their schedule or who suits up, but in watching the defense it’s clear things have begun to click and they’re responding far better to in-game adversity. It was a banner day for the pass rush, which claimed four more sacks. The unit was led by rookie edge rusher T.J. Parker, who notched a pair to increase his total to three on the season. It’s true that it wasn’t Allen’s finest day at the office, with him completing just 11-of-21 passes for 196 yards with one touchdown and one interception. His numbers were propped up by two longs passes: a 54-yard catch and run by tight end Dalton Kincaid, and a 45-yard deep shot to wide receiver DJ Moore. Importantly, the Jets were unable to stop Allen’s threat as a short-yardage runner, which allowed the offense to stay on the field and gave him another pair of rushing touchdowns. With 90 rushing touchdowns, Allen is now just nine touchdowns shy of tying Pro Football Hall of Fame running back Barry Sanders. As for running back James Cook III? What a tremendous game, which sounds like a broken record at this point. Cook had 13 carries for 56 yards at halftime. He finished with 18 carries for 157 yards and a career-long 74-yard touchdown run late in action. Do the math and you’ll see that he had just five carries and 101 yards with that touchdown in the second half. He probably would have had a receiving touchdown as well, if not for a dropped catch. Cook is on a mission in 2026, and Bills Mafia should enjoy every second of his play. The rushing attack is again the story on offense, out-gaining the passing attack and finishing with a total of 201 yards on 32 carries. That’s a machine built for winter football, and Buffalo has an offensive line filled with aggressive run blockers. If they can cut down on the pre-snap penalties, teams may struggle getting the Bills’ offense off the field. Improving to 8-1 was the Buffalo’s ultimate goal in Week 10, which allows them to maintain their first-place lead in the AFC playoff race. Just over half of the 2026 NFL season is now in the books, and the contenders have begun to separate from the pack. The Bills have a still-undefeated road record this season, improving to 5-0 Sunday afternoon. Teams facing Buffalo seem incapable of holding them under 30 points, which often spells doom in professional football. To this point, only the New England Patriots have kept the Bills under 30 — defeating Buffalo 29-26 in Week 4. For as dominant as the Bills have been this season, it feels like their best is yet to come. They’ll need to continue willing teams to submission via the ground attack while trying to improve efficiency in the passing game. In Week 11, Buffalo gets its first crack at this year’s version of the Miami Dolphins. Despite a losing record, Miami is likely to have some things up its sleeve in an effort to frustrate the Bills. Buffalo needs to remain focused and avoid any scent of a letdown before their game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night.

teamStories.summary: — Drew Lock passed for 240 yards and two touchdowns, including a game-breaking 71-yard scoring toss to Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and the Seattle Seahawks beat Las Vegas 21-13 on Sunday to spoil the debut start of Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza.
teamStories.detailText: LAS VEGAS -- — Drew Lock passed for 240 yards and two touchdowns, including a game-breaking 71-yard scoring toss to Jaxon Smith-Njigba , and the Seattle Seahawks beat Las Vegas 21-13 on Sunday to spoil the debut start of Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza . The defending Super Bowl champion but injury-riddled Seahawks (6-4), playing their first regular-season game at Allegiant Stadium, have won three of four entering their bye week. Las Vegas (4-6), which lost standout tight end Brock Bowers to a right ankle injury , has lost six of seven. Facing Seattle's Dark Side defense, even in the venue known as the “Death Star,” figured to be a demanding obstacle for Mendoza. The top pick in this year's draft, elevated after Kirk Cousins was traded Tuesday to Minnesota, looked sharp early in leading the Raiders to 10 points on their first two drives. But then the Seahawks suffocated Mendoza, sacking him six times and holding him to 143 yards passing. Mendoza relied on his legs, rushing six times for 22 yards, including a 10-yard quarterback draw to punctuate the Raiders' first drive. Though Mendoza might one day become a star for the Raiders, Lock outdueled him while again filling in for injured starter Sam Darnold . Smith-Njigba will make just about any quarterback look good, and he finished with eight catches for 171 yards. His deep TD catch midway through the third quarter that gave the Seahawks a 21-10 lead. Mendoza was the fifth No. 1 pick to start at quarterback in Week 10 or later in the common-draft era, and none of those QBs won their opening game. It didn't help that the Raiders' already struggling run game again was stifled by a Seattle defense that seldom gives up much on the ground. The Seahawks have gone 39 consecutive games, including the playoffs, without allowing a 100-yard rusher, and Las Vegas as a team rushed for just 65 yards. Las Vegas' much-maligned defense did end a streak of giving up at least 30 points in six straight games. The Raiders hold that record with four other teams. 2 white hats in officiating crew Two referees worked the game, with Bill Vinovich the lead official and Carl Cheffers officially the umpire. Brad Allen had been assigned to be the referee, but the national grounding of flights on Friday and the resulting disruption in air service forced the NFL to make changes to its crews. There appeared to be confusion late in the first half when Vinovich signaled first down for the Raiders, but the officiating crew switched to fourth down. Mendoza picked up the first down on the following play off a scramble. The official statistics had it listed as a first-down play before the snap. Injuries Seahawks: Their banged-up offensive line suffered another setback when RT Abraham Lucas was injured in the second quarter. LG Quenton Nelson (knee) and LT Charles Cross (ankle) were inactive. ... RB George Holani (knee) went out in the first quarter. Up next Seahawks: At San Francisco on Nov. 29. teamStories.detailText: The Seattle Seahawks (6-4) will go into the bye week feeling good. They overcame a slow first half to put away the Las Vegas Raiders (4-6) and send rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza to defeat in his first career NFL start. Seattle trailed 10-7 at the break before unleashing hell on Earth in the second half, racking up over 300 yards of offense after halftime, while the Raiders had negative yards until their last possession. The 21-13 scoreline didn’t accurately reflect the closeness of the game, as Seattle had its wasteful moments that took points off the board. Drew Lock was far more aggressive and inventive than he was last week against the Arizona Cardinals, an indicator that his right elbow is getting better. He threw two spectacular scramble drill touchdowns to Cooper Kupp and Jaxon Smith-Njigba, although he did lose a couple of fumbles on some unusual plays. Lock’s “dagger” was taking a naked bootleg for 15 yards to pick up a first down and deny Vegas any chance of a miracle comeback. Former Seahawks offensive coordinator turned Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak did what he could to get Mendoza comfortable in the first half by spamming easy, quick throws. Mendoza also impressed with how he used his legs to extend plays and even scored on a QB draw. Ultimately, however, with Brock Bowers injured mid-game, there wasn’t much of a chance for Mendoza to shock the world. The Raiders had just 183 yards of total offense while the Seahawks had 382. It was a happy day for the Seahawks-heavy fans at Allegiant Stadium. The downside? Injuries. Lots of them for both the Seahawks and Raiders. teamStories.summary: The Raiders led 10-7 at halftime, but the Seahawks took over in the final 30 minutes.
teamStories.detailText: Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza's first NFL start started with a bang, but the Seahawks slammed the door on him in the second half on Sunday. Mendoza ran for a touchdown to open the game helped the Raiders to a 10-7 lead over the defending champions through 30 minutes of play in Las Vegas. The second half was a very different story, however. The Raiders were shut out until a Matt Gay field goal with 2:04 left to play in the game and the Seahawks scored a pair of touchdowns to pick up a 21-13 win. The victory pushes their record to 6-4 as they head into their bye week and it came after one of the smartest special teams plays we're likely to see this season. After Gay's field goal, Seahawks returner Tory Horton jumped to bat the ensuing kickoff back in bounds rather than let it sail out for a touchback. He also had the presence of mind to tell Rashid Shaheed to return the ball since he stepped out of bounds and couldn't do it himself. The play wound up taking the clock through the two-minute warning, which meant the Raiders could only stop the clock twice rather than three times. The Seahawks only ran 17 offensive plays in the first half of the game, but they found their footing behind Zach Charbonnet and Jaxon Smith-Njigba in the second half. Charbonnet ran 12 times for 55 yards and Smith-Njigba continued his remarkable season with seven catches for 160 yards after the break. One of those was a 71-yard touchdown from Drew Lock. All in all, Seattle picked up 274 yards in the final two quarters while holding the Raiders to 27 yards on their final six possessions. They sacked Mendoza four times in the second half and the loss of tight end Brock Bowers to an ankle injury left the rookie without real options in the passing game. Mendoza, who finished 17-of-29 for 143 yards, will now try for his first win in Denver next weekend.

teamStories.detailText: Brock Bowers didn't last long on Sunday afternoon. The Las Vegas Raiders tight end was ruled out of their 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks due to an ankle injury he suffered early in the first quarter. That knocked him out for the majority of Fernando Mendoza's starting debut at Allegiant Stadium . Bowers, in the first quarter of the contest, went up to block Seahawks safety Nick Emmanwori for running back Ashton Jeanty. But as Jeanty cut the other way, Bowers had his legs rolled up on in a pile and he went down awkwardly. Brock Bowers is hurt after this play pic.twitter.com/GnkBHz67nD — Arye Pulli (@AryePulliNFL) November 15, 2026 Bowers remained down for a few moments while the team's training staff helped him, and he then limped to the sideline. Bowers did return to the game briefly after that, which helped lead the way for Mendoza's rushing touchdown to get them on the board. But he left the game again late in the second quarter, and the team ruled him out for good just before the start of the second half with the ankle injury. Clearly, it was just too much for him to overcome. Further specifics of his injury are not yet known. Bowers finished with two catches for 18 yards. He entered Sunday with 658 yards and six touchdowns this season, his third in the league after the Raiders took him with the No. 13 overall pick out of Georgia in 2024. Though the Raiders entered the locker room up by a field goal, the Seahawks scored a pair of touchdowns in the third quarter to break the game open. Jadarian Price ran it in from 12 yards out first, and then Jaxon Smith-Njigba hauled in a 71-yard pass from Drew Lock to give Seattle an 11-point lead at the time. BIG PLAY JSN 😮‍💨 @jaxon_smith1 71 YARDS TO THE HOUSE. 📺: @NFLonCBS pic.twitter.com/0sDwRbuiOK — Seattle Seahawks (@Seahawks) November 15, 2026 That was enough to secure the eight-point win. Lock ended up going 14-of-17 for 240 yards with two touchdowns in the win for Seattle, which improved to 6-4 on the season. Zach Charbonnet had 94 rushing yards on two carries, and Smith-Njigba had 171 yards and a score on eight catches. The Raiders dealt away quarterback Kirk Cousins at the deadline, which paved the way for Mendoza, the former Indiana star and reigning Heisman Trophy winner, to get the first start of his career. Mendoza went 17-of-29 for 143 yards in the loss. Mike Washington led them on the ground with 23 yards, and Jeanty had 46 receiving yards on four catches. The Raiders now sit at 5-5 on the year. Though Mendoza appears to be holding his own so far, losing a target like Bowers for any substantial amount of time will make things much more difficult for him as his NFL career gets going.
